# Easykonnet API Guide for App Developers

Everything the mobile app and the admin dashboard need to work with the Easykonnet backend: how to connect and sign in, every GraphQL query and mutation with its arguments, example payloads, success responses and errors, the realtime events, and the REST endpoints.

- Matches the backend code as of 12 September 2026.
- Covers all 98 queries, 128 mutations, 18 realtime events and 5 REST endpoints.
- For code generation, use `schema.graphql` at the repository root (introspection is turned off in production).
- The older guides in `docs/` (FRONTEND_INTEGRATION.md, API_EXAMPLES.md, QUICKSTART.md, PAYMENT_INTEGRATION.md and `docs/api/`) are out of date. Use this one.

# Part 1: Foundations

## Start here

### What the backend offers

Easykonnet's backend serves the mobile app (customers and providers) and the admin dashboard. It covers:

- Accounts: sign-up with an emailed code, sign-in, password reset, profile, settings, deactivation.
- Both sides of the marketplace: customers (`SERVICE_USER`) book; a customer can become a provider (`SERVICE_PROVIDER`), get verified by an admin and list services.
- Discovery: categories, services, provider profiles, nearby search, favourites and likes.
- Bookings from request to completion, with reviews and disputes.
- Payments through Paystack checkout or the in-app wallet. Money is held in escrow, then released to the provider's wallet. Providers add bank accounts and withdraw, by hand or on a schedule.
- Chat, in-app notifications, push notifications (OneSignal) and real-time events (Socket.IO).
- Safety: reports, blocking, a content filter and community terms.
- Admin work: user and provider management, verification and moderation, bans and restrictions, disputes, refunds, withdrawals, analytics, audit logs and broadcasts.

The app does all of this through one GraphQL endpoint. The only other routes the app deals with are Paystack's return page and Socket.IO (see [REST endpoints](#rest-endpoints)).

### Base URLs

| Environment | GraphQL endpoint |
|---|---|
| Production (current) | `https://backend-ehtm.onrender.com/api/graphql` |
| Production (planned domain) | `https://api.easykonnet.com/api/graphql`. This is the API domain `docs/SETUP_CHECKLIST.md` names. Use it once it's live. |
| Local | `http://localhost:3000/api/graphql` (`npm run dev:ws` runs the API with Socket.IO and background jobs; `npm run dev` runs the API only) |

Outside production (`NODE_ENV` not `production`), introspection is on, opening the endpoint in a browser shows Apollo Sandbox, error messages aren't hidden, stack traces are included and CORS allows any origin.

### The server may be asleep

Production runs on Render's free plan. The service sleeps after about 15 minutes without traffic, and the first request after that can take about a minute while it starts. So:

- Give the first request of a session a long timeout (90 seconds is safe). React Native's `fetch` has no timeout of its own, so use an `AbortController`.
- Show a "connecting" state instead of an error while it wakes.
- To wake it early, for example when the app opens, POST this query:

```graphql
query Ping {
  __typename
}
```

The response is `{"data":{"__typename":"Query"}}`.

### HTTP methods

| Method | Use |
|---|---|
| `POST` | The normal way. The body is JSON: `{"query": "...", "variables": {...}, "operationName": "..."}`. |
| `GET` with a `query` search parameter | Queries only. See [GET requests](#get-requests) for the extra header it needs. Browsers can't use it cross-origin. |
| `GET` without `query` | Passed straight to Apollo, skipping the blocklist, complexity and rate-limit checks. Apollo answers **400** `BAD_REQUEST` with its CSRF message, because the request has neither a `Content-Type` nor a preflight header. It isn't a health check: call [`GET /api/health`](#health-check-apihealth) to see whether the server is up, or send `Ping` above to test GraphQL. |
| `OPTIONS` | CORS preflight. Answers `204` with the CORS headers. |
| Anything else | `405`, from Next.js. |

### Headers

| Header | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` | Required on POST, and it must be exactly this value. `application/json; charset=utf-8` gets **400** `BAD_REQUEST` "POST body missing, invalid Content-Type, or JSON object has no keys." A missing header, `text/plain` or a form type gets 400 `BAD_REQUEST` with the CSRF message. Apollo Client and `fetch` with the header set by hand both send the exact value. Don't send `Content-Type` on GET: `application/json` on a GET crashes the handler (HTTP 500). |
| `Authorization` | `Bearer <accessToken>` | Optional. `Bearer` needs a capital B and one space. See [Sending the access token](#sending-the-access-token). |
| `apollo-require-preflight` | `true` | GET only. `x-apollo-operation-name: <name>` works instead. |

The API doesn't use cookies.

### CORS

Mobile apps aren't affected by CORS. For the admin dashboard in a browser:

- In production with `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` set on the server, a listed `Origin` is echoed back in `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. Any other origin gets the first listed origin back, so the browser blocks the response. Ask the backend owner to add the dashboard's origin.
- If `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is empty, or outside production, the response has `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: false`.
- `Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, OPTIONS`.
- `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Authorization, X-Requested-With`. Any other request header fails the preflight. That includes `apollo-require-preflight`, so browsers can't use GET, and Apollo Client's `apollographql-client-name` and `apollographql-client-version`, so don't set a client name or version in the dashboard.
- `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset`, so browser code can read the rate-limit headers.
- `Access-Control-Max-Age: 86400`.

Every response from `/api/graphql` carries these headers, errors included, except the HTTP 500 described in [HTTP-level errors](#http-level-errors).

### Request size

A POST body can be up to 1 MB (1,048,576 bytes). A request whose operation uploads files ([`uploadProfilePhoto`](#uploadprofilephoto), [`uploadProviderImages`](#uploadproviderimages), [`uploadServiceImages`](#uploadserviceimages), [`uploadProviderDocuments`](#uploadproviderdocuments)) can be up to 20 MB. Anything larger is rejected with **413**:

```json
{"errors":[{"message":"Request body too large","extensions":{"code":"PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE"}}]}
```

A `Content-Length` over 20 MB is refused before the body is read. Smaller bodies are read first, so the 1 MB rule applies whether or not `Content-Length` is sent. For file sizes, see [Upload request size](#upload-request-size).

### Schema and generated types

Introspection is off in production. An introspection query gets **400** `GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED`: "GraphQL introspection is not allowed by Apollo Server, but the query contained __schema or __type. To enable introspection, pass introspection: true to ApolloServer in production" (with `extensions.validationErrorCode: "INTROSPECTION_DISABLED"`).

Generate types from `schema.graphql` at the root of the backend repository instead. In the current working tree it matches the schema the server runs (`src/graphql/schemas/index.ts`) exactly. Copy it into the app and refresh the copy when the backend changes. With GraphQL Code Generator:

```ts
// codegen.ts
import type { CodegenConfig } from '@graphql-codegen/cli';

const config: CodegenConfig = {
  schema: './schema.graphql', // copied from the backend repository
  documents: ['src/**/*.{ts,tsx}'],
  generates: {
    './src/gql/': { preset: 'client' },
  },
};

export default config;
```

The schema has no `Subscription` type. Real-time updates come over Socket.IO.

### A first request with fetch

```ts
const API_URL = 'https://backend-ehtm.onrender.com/api/graphql';

async function graphql(query: string, variables?: object, accessToken?: string) {
  const response = await fetch(API_URL, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json', // exactly this value
      ...(accessToken ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` } : {}),
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ query, variables }),
  });

  // 400, 403, 405, 413 and 429 still carry { errors: [...] }; a 500 may not
  if (!response.headers.get('content-type')?.includes('application/json')) {
    throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`);
  }
  const body = await response.json();
  return { status: response.status, retryAfter: response.headers.get('Retry-After'), ...body };
}

const LOGIN = `
  mutation Login($input: LoginInput!) {
    login(input: $input) {
      accessToken
      refreshToken
      user { id email role activeRole status isEmailVerified }
    }
  }
`;

async function signIn(email: string, password: string) {
  const result = await graphql(LOGIN, { input: { email, password } });
  if (result.errors) {
    const [error] = result.errors;
    throw new Error(`${error.extensions?.code}: ${error.message}`);
  }
  const { accessToken, refreshToken } = result.data.login;
  const me = await graphql('query Me { me { id firstName role } }', undefined, accessToken);
  return { accessToken, refreshToken, me: me.data.me };
}
```

### Apollo Client for React and React Native

The simplest setup that handles tokens and rate limits works the same with Apollo Client 3.8+ and 4. Give `HttpLink` a custom `fetch` that:

- sends the access token,
- refreshes it shortly before it expires, and when a response contains `UNAUTHENTICATED`, then retries once,
- signs the user out only when the refresh itself says the session is over,
- waits and retries once on HTTP 429 when `Retry-After` is short.

```ts
// authFetch.ts
const API_URL = 'https://backend-ehtm.onrender.com/api/graphql';
const ADMIN_APP = false; // true in the admin dashboard

type Tokens = { accessToken: string; refreshToken: string };

// Replace with secure storage (Keychain/Keystore via expo-secure-store or react-native-keychain)
export const tokenStore = {
  tokens: null as Tokens | null,
  async get() { return this.tokens; },
  async set(tokens: Tokens | null) { this.tokens = tokens; },
};

let signedOutHandler = () => {};
export const onSignedOut = (handler: () => void) => { signedOutHandler = handler; };

const REFRESH = ADMIN_APP
  ? { field: 'adminRefreshToken', query: 'mutation AdminRefresh($refreshToken: String!) { adminRefreshToken(refreshToken: $refreshToken) { accessToken } }' }
  : { field: 'refreshToken', query: 'mutation Refresh($refreshToken: String!) { refreshToken(refreshToken: $refreshToken) { accessToken } }' };

// Refresh errors that mean the session is over
const SESSION_OVER = ['INVALID_REFRESH_TOKEN', 'INVALID_TOKEN', 'ACCOUNT_INACTIVE', 'NOT_FOUND'];
const MAX_WAIT_SECONDS = 10;

const sleep = (ms: number) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

// Reads exp without verifying (atob is built into browsers and Hermes, React Native 0.74+)
const expiresWithin = (jwt: string, seconds: number) => {
  try {
    const part = jwt.split('.')[1].replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/');
    const { exp } = JSON.parse(atob(part.padEnd(Math.ceil(part.length / 4) * 4, '=')));
    return exp * 1000 - Date.now() < seconds * 1000;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
};

async function send(init: RequestInit, accessToken: string | null): Promise<Response> {
  const headers = new Headers(init.headers);
  headers.set('Content-Type', 'application/json'); // exactly this; a charset parameter is rejected
  if (accessToken) headers.set('Authorization', `Bearer ${accessToken}`);
  else headers.delete('Authorization');

  let response = await fetch(API_URL, { ...init, method: 'POST', headers });
  const wait = Number(response.headers.get('Retry-After'));
  if (response.status === 429 && wait > 0 && wait <= MAX_WAIT_SECONDS) {
    // A 429 means nothing ran, so the same request can be sent again
    await sleep(wait * 1000);
    response = await fetch(API_URL, { ...init, method: 'POST', headers });
  }
  return response;
}

async function refresh(): Promise<string | null> {
  const tokens = await tokenStore.get();
  if (!tokens) return null;

  const response = await send(
    { body: JSON.stringify({ query: REFRESH.query, variables: { refreshToken: tokens.refreshToken } }) },
    null
  );
  if (!response.ok) return null; // 429 or 5xx: keep the session, let this request fail

  const result = await response.json();
  const accessToken: string | undefined = result.data?.[REFRESH.field]?.accessToken;
  if (accessToken) {
    await tokenStore.set({ ...tokens, accessToken }); // the refresh token doesn't change
    return accessToken;
  }
  if (SESSION_OVER.includes(result.errors?.[0]?.extensions?.code)) {
    await tokenStore.set(null);
    signedOutHandler();
  }
  return null;
}

// Concurrent requests share one refresh
let refreshing: Promise<string | null> | null = null;
const refreshOnce = () => (refreshing ??= refresh().finally(() => { refreshing = null; }));

const isUnauthenticated = (body: any) =>
  body?.errors?.some((error: any) => error?.extensions?.code === 'UNAUTHENTICATED') === true;

export const authFetch = async (_uri: RequestInfo | URL, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
  let accessToken = (await tokenStore.get())?.accessToken ?? null;
  if (accessToken && expiresWithin(accessToken, 60)) {
    accessToken = (await refreshOnce()) ?? accessToken;
  }

  const response = await send(init, accessToken);
  if (!accessToken || !response.ok) return response;

  // A rejected token makes the request anonymous, so protected fields fail with UNAUTHENTICATED
  const body = await response.clone().json().catch(() => null);
  if (!isUnauthenticated(body)) return response;

  const newToken = await refreshOnce();
  return newToken ? send(init, newToken) : response;
};
```

```ts
// client.ts
import { ApolloClient, HttpLink, InMemoryCache } from '@apollo/client';
import { authFetch } from './authFetch';

export const client = new ApolloClient({
  link: new HttpLink({ uri: 'https://backend-ehtm.onrender.com/api/graphql', fetch: authFetch }),
  cache: new InMemoryCache(),
});
```

After [`login`](#login) (or [`adminLogin`](#adminlogin)), save both tokens with `tokenStore.set`. Keep requests as POST: don't turn on `useGETForQueries`, and don't add a persisted-query or batch link. When a 429 isn't retried, Apollo Client reports it as a server error with status 429: `error.networkError.statusCode` in Apollo Client 3, or `ServerError.is(error) && error.statusCode` in Apollo Client 4. Read `Retry-After` from its `response` and tell the user how long to wait.

## Authentication and sessions

### Two ways to sign in

| | Customers and providers (mobile app) | Admins and super admins (dashboard) |
|---|---|---|
| Sign in | [`login`](#login) returns `user`, `accessToken`, `refreshToken` | [`adminLogin`](#adminlogin) returns `admin`, `accessToken`, `refreshToken` |
| Refresh | [`refreshToken`](#refreshtoken) returns `accessToken`, `user` | [`adminRefreshToken`](#adminrefreshtoken) returns `accessToken`, `admin` |
| Sign out | [`logout`](#logout) | [`adminLogout`](#adminlogout) |
| Current account | [`me`](#me) | [`adminMe`](#adminme) |
| Where accounts come from | [`register`](#register), then [`verifyEmail`](#verifyemail) | Created by a super admin with [`createAdmin`](#createadmin), already verified |

```graphql
mutation Login($input: LoginInput!) {
  login(input: $input) {
    accessToken
    refreshToken
    user {
      id
      email
      role
      activeRole
      status
      isEmailVerified
    }
  }
}
```

Variables:

```json
{ "input": { "email": "ada.obi@example.com", "password": "Passw0rd!" } }
```

```graphql
mutation AdminLogin($input: AdminLoginInput!) {
  adminLogin(input: $input) {
    accessToken
    refreshToken
    admin {
      id
      email
      role
      status
    }
  }
}
```

Variables:

```json
{ "input": { "email": "ops.lead@example.com", "password": "Adm1nPass!" } }
```

[`adminLogin`](#adminlogin) answers a customer or provider account like a wrong password (`INVALID_CREDENTIALS`, "Invalid admin credentials"). [`login`](#login) refuses admin accounts with `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`, so the dashboard must use [`adminLogin`](#adminlogin).

Tokens also come from two other operations:

- [`verifyEmail`](#verifyemail) returns `accessToken` and `refreshToken` once the code is right. They work like the tokens from [`login`](#login). Both are `null`, with the message "Email verified successfully! Please sign in to continue.", when the account can't be used yet, for example because it's suspended or banned; [`login`](#login) then shows the reason.
- [`becomeProvider`](#becomeprovider) returns a new pair, because the account's role changes. The old access token stops working at once, so replace both tokens.

### Tokens

Both tokens are JWTs signed with the server's secret (HS256). The app can decode them to read `exp`, but it can't verify them. Payload:

```json
{
  "userId": "64f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1",
  "email": "ada.obi@example.com",
  "role": "SERVICE_USER",
  "typ": "access",
  "jti": "5b1f8a2e-3c4d-4e6f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b",
  "iatMs": 1789171200123,
  "iat": 1789171200,
  "exp": 1789776000
}
```

- `jti` identifies the token so [`logout`](#logout) can revoke it, and `iatMs` is the issue time in milliseconds. The app doesn't need either.
- `typ` is `access` or `refresh`. Tokens from [`adminLogin`](#adminlogin) and [`adminRefreshToken`](#adminrefreshtoken) also carry `"isAdmin": true`. `activeRole` isn't in the token.
- Access tokens last `JWT_EXPIRES_IN`: 7 days by default, and `render.yaml` sets `7d`.
- Refresh tokens last `JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN`: 30 days by default, and `render.yaml` sets `30d`. The server keeps its record of a customer or provider refresh token for 30 days, whatever that setting is.
- A refresh token sent as `Authorization: Bearer` is treated like no token. An access token sent to a refresh mutation is rejected. A token without `typ` (issued by older versions) is rejected everywhere, so those users must sign in again.

### Sending the access token

Send `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` on every request. The server never rejects a request because of its token, and `/api/graphql` never answers 401. It decides who is calling like this:

| What the request carries | The request runs as |
|---|---|
| No `Authorization` header, or one that doesn't start with `Bearer ` (for example `bearer ...`) | Anonymous |
| A token with a bad signature, an expired token, or a refresh token | Anonymous |
| A valid access token signed out with [`logout`](#logout) | Anonymous |
| A valid access token issued before the account's sessions were ended: a password change or reset, deactivation, a ban, or an admin ending them | Anonymous |
| A valid access token for an account that no longer exists, is `SUSPENDED` or `DEACTIVATED`, or has an active ban | Anonymous |
| A valid access token whose `role` no longer matches the account's role (after [`becomeProvider`](#becomeprovider) or [`updateAdminRole`](#updateadminrole)) | Anonymous |
| A valid access token for an `ACTIVE` or `PENDING` account, restricted or not | Signed in |

Anonymous requests still run. Public operations such as [`services`](#services) work, with a few differences: a provider's `documents` come back empty and a reviewer's `email` comes back `null`. Any operation that needs a signed-in user fails with:

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "You must be logged in to perform this action",
      "locations": [{ "line": 2, "column": 3 }],
      "path": ["me"],
      "extensions": { "code": "UNAUTHENTICATED" }
    }
  ],
  "data": { "me": null }
}
```

The HTTP status is 200. There is no separate "expired" error: `TOKEN_EXPIRED` and `TOKEN_INVALID` are defined but never sent. So refresh on `UNAUTHENTICATED` when you sent a token, and refresh ahead of `exp` so public screens don't quietly run anonymous.

If Redis is unreachable, a token signed out with [`logout`](#logout) is accepted until Redis is back. The other checks, including ended sessions, still run.

For rate limiting, a request counts as signed in whenever its access token has a valid signature, is unexpired and has `typ: access`, even if the account checks above then make it anonymous. See [General limits](#general-limits).

Socket.IO accepts the same access token and applies the same checks when connecting, and again about every 5 minutes while connected.

### Refreshing

**Customers and providers.** Call [`refreshToken`](#refreshtoken):

```graphql
mutation Refresh($refreshToken: String!) {
  refreshToken(refreshToken: $refreshToken) {
    accessToken
    user {
      id
      role
      activeRole
      status
    }
  }
}
```

Variables:

```json
{ "refreshToken": "<refresh token from login>" }
```

The server checks, in order:

1. The server recorded this refresh token and it hasn't been revoked. [`login`](#login), [`verifyEmail`](#verifyemail) and [`becomeProvider`](#becomeprovider) record refresh tokens. While Redis is unreachable this check is skipped, and a validly signed, unexpired refresh token is accepted.
2. It's a valid, unexpired refresh token.
3. It belongs to the same user.
4. The account exists, isn't an admin account, is `ACTIVE`, isn't banned, and its sessions weren't ended after the token was issued.

The new access token carries the account's current role.

There is **no rotation**. The response has no new refresh token, and the one you have keeps working until it expires or [`logout`](#logout) revokes it. Keep it.

Every failure has the code `INVALID_REFRESH_TOKEN`:

| Message | Cause |
|---|---|
| Refresh token has been invalidated | Not recorded, revoked by [`logout`](#logout) or by ending all sessions, or an access token sent instead |
| Token mismatch | The recorded user differs from the token's user |
| Invalid refresh token | The account is gone, is an admin account, isn't `ACTIVE` (suspended, deactivated, pending), or is banned |
| Invalid or expired refresh token | Bad signature, expired, or wrong `typ` |

The exact message for every case, including sessions ended after the token was issued, is listed under [`refreshToken`](#refreshtoken).

**Admins.** Call [`adminRefreshToken`](#adminrefreshtoken):

```graphql
mutation AdminRefresh($refreshToken: String!) {
  adminRefreshToken(refreshToken: $refreshToken) {
    accessToken
    admin {
      id
      role
    }
  }
}
```

Variables:

```json
{ "refreshToken": "<refresh token from adminLogin>" }
```

The token must be a valid refresh token carrying `isAdmin` and an admin role. The admin must still exist with an admin role, be `ACTIVE` and not be banned. The server keeps no record of admin refresh tokens, so they work until they expire. Errors:

| Code | Message |
|---|---|
| `INVALID_TOKEN` | Invalid admin token (not an admin token) / Invalid or expired token |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Admin not found |
| `ACCOUNT_INACTIVE` | Admin account is not active |

**When to refresh:** shortly before `exp`, and once after an `UNAUTHENTICATED` error on a request that carried a token. Refreshing has its own limit of 120 per minute per IP, or per user when a valid access token is sent. Make one refresh at a time and share its result across waiting requests, as the Apollo setup above does. On any of the failure codes above, clear the tokens and show the sign-in screen. On a network error, 429 or 5xx, keep the tokens and try later.

### What ends or changes a session

| Event | Access tokens already issued | Refresh tokens | Signing in afterwards |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`logout`](#logout) with `refreshToken` | The access token sent with the request stops working at once; others keep working | The refresh token passed is revoked; others aren't | Works |
| [`logout`](#logout) without `refreshToken` | The access token sent with the request stops working at once; others keep working | Nothing is revoked | Works |
| [`adminLogout`](#adminlogout) | The access token sent with the request stops working at once; others keep working | The refresh token passed is revoked; others aren't | Works |
| [`changePassword`](#changepassword) or [`resetPassword`](#resetpassword) | Every token issued before the change becomes anonymous | Revoked | New password |
| [`adminChangePassword`](#adminchangepassword) or [`adminResetPassword`](#adminresetpassword) | Every token issued before the change becomes anonymous, including the caller's | Revoked | New password |
| [`banUser`](#banuser) | Anonymous: banning ends every session, and those sessions stay ended after the ban ends or is lifted | Refused, also after the ban ends | `ACCOUNT_BANNED` while the ban lasts; a ban with a `days` value ends by itself |
| [`suspendUser`](#suspenduser) or [`suspendAdmin`](#suspendadmin) (status `SUSPENDED`) | Anonymous | Refresh fails | `USER_SUSPENDED` / `ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED` |
| [`deactivateMyAccount`](#deactivatemyaccount) (status `DEACTIVATED`) | Anonymous: deactivating ends every session | Revoked | Signing in with the correct password reactivates the account |
| [`restrictUser`](#restrictuser) | Keep working | Keep working | Works; payments and withdrawals fail with `ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED` |
| Role change: [`becomeProvider`](#becomeprovider), [`updateAdminRole`](#updateadminrole) | Anonymous | Refresh returns a token with the new role | Works |

Notes:

- [`logout`](#logout) and [`adminLogout`](#adminlogout) need a working access token; otherwise they return `UNAUTHENTICATED`. When signing out, send the refresh token to [`logout`](#logout), unregister push first (see [Push notifications](#push-notifications)), then delete both tokens locally whatever the result.
- A deactivated user reactivates by signing in again with the correct password. [`reactivateMyAccount`](#reactivatemyaccount) still exists, but a deactivated account has no session to call it from. An admin can also run [`activateUser`](#activateuser).
- [`unbanUser`](#unbanuser), [`removeRestriction`](#removerestriction), [`activateUser`](#activateuser) and [`activateAdmin`](#activateadmin) lift the matching state. After a suspension, tokens that haven't expired work again, and so does refreshing. After a ban or deactivation, earlier sessions stay ended and the user signs in again.

### Account statuses and flags

`User.status` is one of `PENDING`, `ACTIVE`, `SUSPENDED`, `DEACTIVATED`. Bans, restrictions and email verification are separate flags.

| State | How it happens | [`login`](#login) returns | [`adminLogin`](#adminlogin) returns | A signed-in session |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PENDING`, email not verified | [`register`](#register) | `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED`: "Please verify your email before logging in. Check your inbox for the verification code." with `extensions.requiresVerification: true` | n/a | No tokens exist yet. [`verifyEmail`](#verifyemail) makes the account `ACTIVE`. |
| `ACTIVE` | Verified email, or created by a super admin | Tokens | Tokens | Works |
| `SUSPENDED` | [`suspendUser`](#suspenduser), [`suspendAdmin`](#suspendadmin) | `USER_SUSPENDED`: "Your account has been suspended. Please contact support." | `ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED`: "Your admin account has been suspended." | Anonymous |
| `DEACTIVATED` | [`deactivateMyAccount`](#deactivatemyaccount) | Tokens: signing in with the correct password reactivates the account | `ACCOUNT_DEACTIVATED`: "Your admin account has been deactivated." | Anonymous: deactivating ends every session |
| Banned (`bannedAt` set, `bannedUntil` empty or in the future) | [`banUser`](#banuser) | `ACCOUNT_BANNED`: "Your account has been banned. Please contact support." | `ACCOUNT_BANNED`: "Your admin account has been banned." | Anonymous |
| Restricted (`restrictedAt` set, `restrictedUntil` in the future) | [`restrictUser`](#restrictuser) | Tokens | Tokens | Works, except [`initializePayment`](#initializepayment) and [`payWithWallet`](#paywithwallet) (`ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED`: "Your account is restricted, so you can’t make payments right now.") and [`requestWithdrawal`](#requestwithdrawal) (`ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED`: "Your account is restricted, so you can’t withdraw right now. Please contact support.", also returned for a banned account) |
| Locked (too many wrong passwords) | See [Failed sign-ins and lockout](#failed-sign-ins-and-lockout) | `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` | `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` | Unaffected |

Ban and restriction messages both use the curly apostrophe (’) exactly as shown.

Other places the account state matters:

- [`becomeProvider`](#becomeprovider) needs an `ACTIVE` account (`ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE`: "Your account must be active to become a provider") with a verified email (`EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED`: "Please verify your email before becoming a provider").
- [`deactivateMyAccount`](#deactivatemyaccount) only works on `ACTIVE` accounts (`BAD_REQUEST`: "Only active accounts can be deactivated"). [`reactivateMyAccount`](#reactivatemyaccount) only works on `DEACTIVATED` ones (`BAD_REQUEST`: "Account is not deactivated").
- Registering again with an email that isn't verified yet sends a new code; the pending account's name, phone and password aren't changed. A verified email gets `USER_ALREADY_EXISTS`: "A user with this email already exists".

[`login`](#login) runs its checks in this order:

1. Input validation (`VALIDATION_ERROR`)
2. The per-email attempt limit (`RATE_LIMITED`)
3. Unknown email, admin account or wrong password (`INVALID_CREDENTIALS`)
4. Locked
5. Email not verified
6. Suspended
7. Banned

Steps 4 to 7 only answer once the password is right. A deactivated account is reactivated at that point and signed in.

[`adminLogin`](#adminlogin) checks the password first: an unknown email, a customer, provider or deleted account, or a wrong password all get `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` "Invalid admin credentials". With the correct password it then answers locked, suspended, deactivated, banned.

### Failed sign-ins and lockout

- Each wrong password adds one to the account's failed-attempt count. On [`login`](#login), the error is `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` "Invalid email or password" with `extensions.attemptsRemaining` (4, 3, 2, 1 with the defaults).
- The attempt that reaches `MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS` (default 5) locks the account for `LOCKOUT_DURATION_MINUTES` (default 30). [`login`](#login) answers `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` "Account locked due to too many failed attempts. Please try again in 30 minutes." [`adminLogin`](#adminlogin) still answers `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` on that attempt.
- While locked, [`login`](#login) answers `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` "Account is locked due to too many failed attempts. Please try again in N minutes." only when the password is right; a wrong password gets `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` without `attemptsRemaining`. [`adminLogin`](#adminlogin) answers `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` "Account is locked. Try again in N minutes."
- The count resets on a successful sign-in, on [`resetPassword`](#resetpassword) / [`adminResetPassword`](#adminresetpassword), and when a lockout ends. Offer "Forgot password" on `ACCOUNT_LOCKED`.
- Wrong current passwords sent to [`changePassword`](#changepassword), [`adminChangePassword`](#adminchangepassword) and [`deleteAccount`](#deleteaccount) count towards the lockout too, and while the account is locked those mutations answer `ACCOUNT_LOCKED`. A successful [`adminChangePassword`](#adminchangepassword) resets the count.
- [`login`](#login) also has a per-email attempt limit: after 5 failed sign-ins within 5 minutes, the next attempt is blocked for 15 minutes (`RATE_LIMITED`). Both sign-in mutations also share a limit of 10 requests per 15 minutes per email or signed-in user, and 100 per 15 minutes per IP (HTTP 429). See [Rate limits and request limits](#rate-limits-and-request-limits).

### Roles and activeRole

| Role | Who |
|---|---|
| `SERVICE_USER` | Customers. Every registration starts here. |
| `SERVICE_PROVIDER` | Customers who ran [`becomeProvider`](#becomeprovider). They can still book services. |
| `ADMIN` | Moderators and support staff |
| `SUPER_ADMIN` | Admins who also manage admins, money and platform settings |

Operations check roles in one of four ways:

- **Signed in:** any role.
- **Minimum role**, in the order `SERVICE_USER` < `SERVICE_PROVIDER` < `ADMIN` < `SUPER_ADMIN`. A provider passes customer checks.
- **Exactly `SERVICE_PROVIDER`**, for provider operations. Admins get `UNAUTHORIZED` there, and a provider account without a provider profile gets `PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND` "Provider profile not found".
- **Exactly `ADMIN` or `SUPER_ADMIN`.**

A failed role check returns `UNAUTHORIZED`: "You do not have permission to perform this action". Checks on a specific record (your own booking, your own service) return `FORBIDDEN` or `NOT_FOUND` with their own messages. Role checks use the role in the token, which must match the account's current role.

`activeRole` lets a provider switch the app between customer mode and provider mode:

- It's stored on the account and returned as `User.activeRole` by [`login`](#login), [`refreshToken`](#refreshtoken) and [`me`](#me). Until a provider switches, it equals `role`.
- [`switchActiveRole`](#switchactiverole) sets it to `SERVICE_USER` or `SERVICE_PROVIDER`, for `SERVICE_PROVIDER` accounts with a provider profile (the same rule as `canSwitch`). [`myActiveRole`](#myactiverole) reports `currentRole`, `activeRole`, `canSwitch` and `hasProviderProfile`.
- It's a display mode only. It isn't in the token, switching doesn't need new tokens, and the server doesn't use it for access checks. A provider can call customer operations in either mode.

```graphql
mutation SwitchMode($targetRole: UserRole!) {
  switchActiveRole(targetRole: $targetRole) {
    id
    role
    activeRole
  }
}
```

Variables:

```json
{ "targetRole": "SERVICE_USER" }
```

## Making requests

### Request body

```json
{
  "query": "query Me { me { id firstName role } }",
  "variables": {},
  "operationName": "Me"
}
```

- `query` is required. `variables` must be a JSON object, not a JSON-encoded string. `operationName` must be a string.
- Name your operations. With more than one operation in a document, `operationName` must pick one. Otherwise Apollo answers **400** `OPERATION_RESOLUTION_FAILURE` with "Must provide operation name if query contains multiple operations." or "Unknown operation named "B".".
- A body that is empty, `{}`, or isn't an object gets **400** `BAD_REQUEST` "POST body missing, invalid Content-Type, or JSON object has no keys." A body that isn't valid JSON at all crashes the handler and returns HTTP 500 with no GraphQL body.
- Variables are checked against the schema before anything runs. Wrong types or missing required variables get **400** `BAD_USER_INPUT`, for example "Variable "$id" of required type "ID!" was not provided."

### Responses

- The body is `{"data": ..., "errors": [...]}`, with either part possibly absent.
- Errors from running an operation come back with HTTP **200**. `data` may be partial: a failed nullable field becomes `null`, and a failed non-null field makes its parent `null`, up to `"data": null`.
- Put one mutation in each request. Root fields in a request run independently, so one can succeed while another fails.

### GET requests

GET works for queries:

```text
GET /api/graphql?query=query%20Ping%20%7B%20__typename%20%7D&operationName=Ping
apollo-require-preflight: true
```

- Pass `query`, and optionally `operationName`, `variables` (URL-encoded JSON) and `extensions`, each at most once.
- Send `apollo-require-preflight: true`, or `x-apollo-operation-name`, and no `Content-Type`. Without the preflight header, Apollo answers **400** `BAD_REQUEST`: "This operation has been blocked as a potential Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF). Please either specify a 'content-type' header (with a type that is not one of application/x-www-form-urlencoded, multipart/form-data, text/plain) or provide a non-empty value for one of the following headers: x-apollo-operation-name, apollo-require-preflight". A GET with `Content-Type: application/json` returns HTTP 500.
- Mutations over GET get **405** `BAD_REQUEST` "GET requests only support query operations, not mutation operations" with `Allow: POST`.
- The blocklist, complexity limits and rate limits apply as for POST; only the 1 MB size check is POST-only.
- Browsers can't send the preflight header cross-origin (see [CORS](#cors)), so the dashboard must use POST.

### No persisted queries or batching

- Automatic persisted queries are off, so every request must carry the full query text. A request with `extensions.persistedQuery` gets HTTP **200** with `{"errors":[{"message":"PersistedQueryNotSupported","extensions":{"code":"PERSISTED_QUERY_NOT_SUPPORTED"}}]}`. Don't add a persisted-query link.
- Batched requests (a JSON array of operations) get **400** `BAD_REQUEST` "Operation batching disabled."

### Complexity limits

Before running a request, the server parses it and measures three things. Over any limit, it answers **400** without running anything and without counting the request against rate limits:

```json
{"errors":[{"message":"Query depth 11 exceeds maximum allowed depth of 10","extensions":{"code":"QUERY_TOO_COMPLEX"}}]}
```

| Measure | Limit (setting) | How it's counted | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| Depth | 10 (`GRAPHQL_MAX_DEPTH`) | Nested selection sets, counting the operation's own braces: `{ __typename }` is 1, `{ me { id } }` is 2. Named and inline fragments count as if their fields were written in place. | Query depth N exceeds maximum allowed depth of 10 |
| Root fields | 20 (`GRAPHQL_MAX_ROOT_FIELDS`) | Every top-level field occurrence: aliased copies, `__typename`, and fields that fragments spread at the top level. | A request may select at most 20 root fields |
| Aliases | 30 (`GRAPHQL_MAX_ALIASES`) | Every alias at any depth. A fragment's aliases count each time it's spread. | A request may use at most 30 aliases |

More notes:

- If `operationName` doesn't pick exactly one operation, all operations in the document are measured together.
- A chain of fragments deep enough to overflow the server's measurement gets "Query is too complex".
- A query that doesn't parse skips these checks. Apollo then answers `GRAPHQL_PARSE_FAILED`, and the request does count against the general rate limit.

If one of the app's own screens hits a limit, split the query or ask for the setting to be raised.

### IDs

Every `ID` is a MongoDB ObjectId: a 24-character hexadecimal string such as `"64f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1"`. Operations don't check the format before querying. A malformed ID usually comes back as `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` "An internal error occurred" instead of a validation error. Check IDs in the app with `/^[0-9a-fA-F]{24}$/` before sending them.

## Errors

### Error shape

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "Invalid email or password",
      "locations": [{ "line": 2, "column": 3 }],
      "path": ["login"],
      "extensions": { "code": "INVALID_CREDENTIALS", "attemptsRemaining": 3 }
    }
  ],
  "data": null
}
```

- Branch on `errors[i].extensions.code`, never on the message text.
- `locations` and `path` point at the failing field. They're absent on request-level errors.
- Some errors add fields to `extensions`:

| Code | Extra fields in `extensions` |
|---|---|
| `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` from [`login`](#login) | `attemptsRemaining` |
| `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED` from [`login`](#login) | `requiresVerification: true` |
| `RATE_LIMITED` from operations | `resetIn` (seconds), `blocked` |
| `GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED` for introspection | `validationErrorCode: "INTROSPECTION_DISABLED"` |

- Outside production, `extensions.stacktrace` is included.

### HTTP-level errors

These are decided before GraphQL runs, or by Apollo for a malformed request. Every response has the same `errors` body and carries the CORS headers.

| Status | Code | Message | When | Extra headers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `QUERY_TOO_COMPLEX` | See [Complexity limits](#complexity-limits) | Too deep, too many root fields or aliases | None |
| 400 | `BAD_REQUEST` | CSRF message; "POST body missing, invalid Content-Type, or JSON object has no keys."; "Operation batching disabled." | Wrong or missing `Content-Type` (`application/json` is right, with or without a charset), empty body, batch, GET without the preflight header or without `query` | Rate-limit headers (not on GET without `query`) |
| 400 | `BAD_REQUEST` | The request body is not valid JSON | A POST body that isn't valid JSON | None |
| 400 | `GRAPHQL_PARSE_FAILED`, `GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED`, `BAD_USER_INPUT`, `OPERATION_RESOLUTION_FAILURE` | Apollo's text | See [Apollo's own error codes](#apollos-own-error-codes) | Rate-limit headers |
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` | Access denied | The client IP is on the server's blocklist (set by an operator) | None |
| 405 | `BAD_REQUEST` | GET requests only support query operations, not mutation operations | Mutation over GET | `Allow: POST`, rate-limit headers |
| 413 | `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | Request body too large | POST body over 1 MB, or over 20 MB for a request that uploads files | None |
| 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` | Too many requests. Please try again in N seconds. | A rate limit was hit; nothing ran | `Retry-After`, `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset` |

The server's own responses (400 `QUERY_TOO_COMPLEX` and invalid JSON, 403, 413, 429) use `Content-Type: application/json`. Apollo's use `application/json; charset=utf-8`.

Example 429:

```text
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 900
X-RateLimit-Limit: 10
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 10
X-RateLimit-Reset: 900

{"errors":[{"message":"Too many requests. Please try again in 900 seconds.","extensions":{"code":"RATE_LIMITED"}}]}
```

### Apollo's own error codes

| Code | HTTP | Example message | Cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GRAPHQL_PARSE_FAILED` | 400 | Syntax Error: Expected Name, found &lt;EOF&gt;. | The query text isn't valid GraphQL |
| `GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED` | 400 | Cannot query field "nope" on type "User". Did you mean "role"? | The query doesn't match the schema, or uses introspection in production |
| `BAD_USER_INPUT` | 400 | Variable "$id" got invalid value { a: 1 }; ID cannot represent value: { a: 1 } | Variables don't match their declared types. No resolver throws this code. |
| `OPERATION_RESOLUTION_FAILURE` | 400 | Must provide operation name if query contains multiple operations. | `operationName` missing or unknown |
| `BAD_REQUEST` | 400/405 | See the table above | Malformed HTTP request |
| `PERSISTED_QUERY_NOT_SUPPORTED` | 200 | PersistedQueryNotSupported | `extensions.persistedQuery` sent |
| `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` | 200 | An internal error occurred | An unexpected failure while running a field: a database error, a malformed ID, a bug |

### What production hides

In production (`NODE_ENV=production`, as on Render), the server changes exactly one kind of error:

- An error with the code `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` is replaced with `{"message":"An internal error occurred","extensions":{"code":"INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR"}}`. `locations` and `path` are dropped too, so the app can't tell which field failed. Any error the backend didn't throw on purpose ends up here.
- Every other error passes through unchanged, with its message and extra `extensions`. That includes every coded error in this chapter, Apollo's request errors and `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

What the app can show:

- **Safe to show:** messages for the account, validation, content and business codes below. They're written for users.
- **Don't show:** `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`, `QUERY_TOO_COMPLEX`, Apollo's codes, `BAD_REQUEST`, and `UPLOAD_FAILED`, whose message is Cloudinary's raw error text. Log these and show a generic message.

Outside production nothing is replaced, and internal error messages and stack traces reach the client. Don't build UI on them.

### Authentication and authorization codes

| Code | Message | Raised by |
|---|---|---|
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` | You must be logged in to perform this action | Any operation that needs sign-in, when the request is anonymous (see [Sending the access token](#sending-the-access-token)) |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | You do not have permission to perform this action | Role checks. Some operations use this code with their own message, for example "You can only pay for your own bookings". |
| `FORBIDDEN` | Access denied (HTTP 403, blocked IP). Operations use this code with their own messages. | Blocklist, record-level checks |
| `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` | Invalid email or password ([`login`](#login)) / Invalid admin credentials ([`adminLogin`](#adminlogin)) | Unknown email, wrong password, or an account of the other kind (admin on [`login`](#login), customer or provider on [`adminLogin`](#adminlogin)) |
| `INVALID_REFRESH_TOKEN` | Refresh token has been invalidated / Token mismatch / Invalid refresh token / Invalid or expired refresh token | [`refreshToken`](#refreshtoken) |
| `INVALID_TOKEN` | Invalid admin token / Invalid or expired token / Refresh token has been invalidated | [`adminRefreshToken`](#adminrefreshtoken) |
| `ACCOUNT_INACTIVE` | Admin account is not active | [`adminRefreshToken`](#adminrefreshtoken) |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Admin not found (from [`adminRefreshToken`](#adminrefreshtoken)); many operations use this code with "X not found" messages | Missing records, or records the caller may not see |

### Account status and posting codes

| Code | Message |
|---|---|
| `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED` | Please verify your email before logging in. Check your inbox for the verification code. / Please verify your email before becoming a provider |
| `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` | Account locked due to too many failed attempts. Please try again in 30 minutes. / Account is locked due to too many failed attempts. Please try again in N minutes. / Account is locked. Try again in N minutes. |
| `USER_SUSPENDED` | Your account has been suspended. Please contact support. |
| `ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED` | Your admin account has been suspended. |
| `ACCOUNT_DEACTIVATED` | Your admin account has been deactivated. |
| `ACCOUNT_BANNED` | Your account has been banned. Please contact support. / Your admin account has been banned. |
| `ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED` | Your account is restricted, so you can’t make payments right now. / Your account is restricted, so you can’t withdraw right now. Please contact support. |
| `ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE` | Your account must be active to become a provider |
| `TERMS_NOT_ACCEPTED` | Please accept the community terms before posting |
| `TERMS_VERSION_OUTDATED` | Please review and accept the current terms (version 2026-09) (the server's `TERMS_VERSION`) |
| `INAPPROPRIATE_CONTENT` | {Field} contains language that isn't allowed on Easykonnet |
| `CONTACT_DETAILS_NOT_ALLOWED` | {Field} can't include phone numbers, email addresses or account numbers. You can share contact details in chat once a booking is made. |
| `RATE_LIMITED` (HTTP 200) | Too many attempts. Please try again in N minutes. ("minute" when N is 1) / Broadcast rate limit reached (50/day). Resets in Ns. |
| `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | Rate limit exceeded. You can verify up to 5 accounts per hour. |

`{Field}` is one of: Your review, Your response, Service name, Description, Business name, Business description, First name, Last name.

### Validation codes

**ID arguments.** Before any operation runs, every argument typed `ID`, including IDs inside input objects and lists, must be a 24-character hexadecimal string. Otherwise nothing runs and the error is `BAD_USER_INPUT` with the message "{argument} is not a valid ID", for example "input.bookingId is not a valid ID" or "messageIds[2] is not a valid ID". `extensions.argument` holds the same path.

**Shared validators** (`src/utils/security.ts`), used across operations:

| Code | Message | Checked on |
|---|---|---|
| `INVALID_INPUT` | {field} must be at least 2 characters / {field} too long (max 100 characters) / {field} contains invalid characters | Person names (first and last): letters, including accented letters, digits, spaces, `-`, `'`, `’` and `.`. Business, service and category names, city, state and country also allow `&` `,` `/` `(` `)`. Other characters such as `!` `@` `%` `;` `<` `>` are rejected. |
| `INVALID_INPUT` | {field} must be at least N characters / {field} must be at most N characters | Descriptions and addresses, measured after HTML tags are removed |
| `INVALID_INPUT` | Rating must be between 1 and 5 | [`createReview`](#createreview) ([`updateReview`](#updatereview) uses `INVALID_RATING` with the same text) |
| `INVALID_INPUT` | {field} must be a number / {field} must be positive / {field} can have at most 2 decimal places | Service price and duration, which must be greater than 0. Admin wallet adjustments use their own `INVALID_AMOUNT` check. |
| `INVALID_INPUT` | Invalid search query | Search text containing MongoDB operators such as `$gt` |
| `INVALID_EMAIL` | Invalid email format / Email too long | Email checks after the schema-level checks |
| `INVALID_PHONE` | Invalid Nigerian phone number | Phone numbers: `0` or `+234`/`234`, then 7, 8 or 9, then 0 or 1, then 8 digits. Spaces and dashes are stripped first, and numbers are stored as `+234` followed by 10 digits. |
| `INVALID_URL` | Invalid URL / URL too long (2048) | `http`/`https` URLs: `updateProfile.profilePhoto`, `updateProviderProfile.profilePhoto`, category icons |
| `WEAK_PASSWORD` | Password must be at least 8 characters / …one uppercase letter / …one lowercase letter / …one number | [`register`](#register). In practice the schema check below catches these first. |

**Schema checks** (`src/utils/validation.ts`, Zod) run on [`register`](#register), [`login`](#login), and the new password of [`resetPassword`](#resetpassword), [`changePassword`](#changepassword), [`createAdmin`](#createadmin), [`adminResetPassword`](#adminresetpassword) and [`adminChangePassword`](#adminchangepassword). The code is `VALIDATION_ERROR`, and the message is only the **first** failing rule. Fields are checked in order (email, password, firstName, lastName, phone), and password rules in the order below:

| Message |
|---|
| Invalid email address |
| Password is required ([`login`](#login)) |
| Password must be at least 8 characters |
| Password must not exceed 128 characters |
| Password must contain at least one uppercase letter |
| Password must contain at least one lowercase letter |
| Password must contain at least one number |
| Password must contain at least one special character (!@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{};':"\|,.<>/?) |
| First name must be at least 2 characters |
| Last name must be at least 2 characters |
| Invalid phone number |

[`register`](#register) and [`updateProfile`](#updateprofile) accept the same phone formats, local (`08031234567`) or international (`+2348031234567`), and store the number as `+2348031234567`.

Other operations throw `VALIDATION_ERROR` or `INVALID_INPUT` with their own messages. The operation reference lists them.

### Codes defined in src/constants

`src/constants/errors.ts` pairs each code with a default message. Only some of these pairs reach the app as written:

| Code | Default message | Sent by the API |
|---|---|---|
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` | You must be logged in to perform this action | Yes, exactly |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | You do not have permission to perform this action | Yes, from role checks; other messages elsewhere |
| `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` | Invalid email or password | Yes, from [`login`](#login); [`adminLogin`](#adminlogin) uses "Invalid admin credentials" |
| `TOKEN_EXPIRED` | Your session has expired. Please log in again | Never |
| `TOKEN_INVALID` | Invalid authentication token | Never |
| `USER_NOT_FOUND` | User not found | Yes, exactly |
| `USER_ALREADY_EXISTS` | A user with this email already exists | Yes, from [`register`](#register); other messages elsewhere |
| `USER_SUSPENDED` | Your account has been suspended | Code only, with "Your account has been suspended. Please contact support." |
| `USER_NOT_VERIFIED` | Please verify your account to continue | Never ([`login`](#login) uses `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED`) |
| `SERVICE_NOT_FOUND` | Service not found | Yes, exactly |
| `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | This service is currently unavailable | Never |
| `BOOKING_NOT_FOUND` | Booking not found | Yes, exactly |
| `BOOKING_ALREADY_EXISTS` | You already have a pending booking for this service | Never |
| `BOOKING_CANCELLED` | This booking has been cancelled | Never |
| `PAYMENT_FAILED` | Payment processing failed | Never as an error code (it's a notification type) |
| `PAYMENT_NOT_FOUND` | Payment record not found | Code only, with "Payment not found" or "Payment not found for this reference" |
| `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` | Insufficient funds to complete this transaction | Never |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Validation failed | Code only, with specific messages |
| `INVALID_INPUT` | Invalid input provided | Code only, with specific messages |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | An unexpected error occurred | Defined, but no operation raises it at the moment |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Resource not found | Code only, with specific messages |
| `BAD_REQUEST` | Bad request | Code only, with specific messages (Apollo uses it too) |
| `FORBIDDEN` | Access forbidden | Code only, with specific messages |

### Codes the app shouldn't see

These codes exist in the backend but can't normally reach the app. They're listed so no code in the source is a mystery.

| Code | Message | Why the app won't see it |
|---|---|---|
| `INVALID_RESOLUTION` | Invalid resolution type. Must be one of: {values} | [`resolveDispute`](#resolvedispute) takes a `DisputeResolution` enum, so GraphQL rejects a bad value first with `BAD_USER_INPUT`. |
| `TOO_MANY_FILES` | Maximum {max} files allowed per upload | The upload mutations check their own limits first (`MAX_IMAGES_EXCEEDED`, `MAX_DOCUMENTS_EXCEEDED`). |
| `DUPLICATE_REFERENCE` | This transaction reference has already been used | An internal safeguard in the wallet ledger. If the app ever receives it, report it to the backend team. |
| `INVALID_SIGNATURE` | Invalid webhook signature | Only for Paystack's webhook calls, answered as HTTP 401. See [Paystack webhook](#paystack-webhook-apiwebhookspaystack). |

### Handling errors in the app

| Code | What to do |
|---|---|
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` | If a token was sent: refresh once and retry. If not signed in: go to sign-in. |
| `INVALID_REFRESH_TOKEN`, `INVALID_TOKEN`, `ACCOUNT_INACTIVE` (from a refresh) | Clear tokens and go to sign-in |
| `UNAUTHORIZED`, `FORBIDDEN` | Don't retry. Show the message, hide the action, and refetch [`me`](#me) if the role may have changed. |
| `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` | Show the message; use `attemptsRemaining` to warn before a lockout |
| `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED` | Open code entry; offer [`resendVerificationOtp`](#resendverificationotp) |
| `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` | Show the message; offer [`forgotPassword`](#forgotpassword) |
| `USER_SUSPENDED`, `ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED`, `ACCOUNT_BANNED` | Show the message and support contact; don't retry |
| `ACCOUNT_DEACTIVATED` | From [`adminLogin`](#adminlogin) only: show the message and the support contact |
| `ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED` | Show the message; disable payment and withdrawal actions |
| `TERMS_NOT_ACCEPTED` | Show the terms, call [`acceptTerms`](#acceptterms) with `termsStatus.currentVersion`, then retry |
| `TERMS_VERSION_OUTDATED` | Refetch [`termsStatus`](#termsstatus) and show the new terms |
| `INAPPROPRIATE_CONTENT`, `CONTACT_DETAILS_NOT_ALLOWED` | Show the message under the field; keep the user's text so they can edit |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR`, `INVALID_INPUT`, `INVALID_EMAIL`, `INVALID_PHONE`, `INVALID_URL`, `WEAK_PASSWORD` | Show the message under the field; apply the same rules before sending |
| `RATE_LIMITED` with HTTP 200 | Show the message; disable the button for `extensions.resetIn` seconds when present |
| HTTP 429 `RATE_LIMITED` | Wait `Retry-After` seconds. Retry automatically if it's short; otherwise tell the user how long. |
| `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | Show the message |
| `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | Compress or resize the file and try again |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Show "not found" and refresh the list it came from |
| `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`, HTTP 500 | Show a generic error. Retry queries with backoff. Before retrying a mutation, check whether it took effect. |
| `QUERY_TOO_COMPLEX`, `GRAPHQL_PARSE_FAILED`, `GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED`, `BAD_USER_INPUT`, `BAD_REQUEST`, `OPERATION_RESOLUTION_FAILURE`, `PERSISTED_QUERY_NOT_SUPPORTED`, `UPLOAD_FAILED` | An app bug or a server issue: log it and show a generic error |
| HTTP 403 `FORBIDDEN` "Access denied" | Show a generic "can't connect" message |

## Rate limits and request limits

General and strict limits (the first two tables below) are counted in Redis, with a sliding window: a request stops counting a full window after it was made. While Redis is unreachable, each server process enforces the same numbers in memory with fixed windows.

### General limits

Every request that carries a GraphQL document (a POST, or a GET with `query`) counts against exactly one general limit:

| Caller | Limit | Counted per |
|---|---|---|
| Signed in, request contains a mutation | 60 per minute | User |
| Signed in, anything else (including requests that don't parse) | 300 per minute | User |
| Not signed in | 300 per minute, queries and mutations together | Client IP |

- "Signed in" here means only that the `Authorization` header holds an access token with a valid signature, unexpired and with `typ: access`. Missing, forged or expired tokens, and refresh tokens, count as not signed in.
- A token for a suspended or banned account still counts against that user's limit, even though the request then runs anonymously.
- Not counted: requests rejected for complexity (400), a blocked IP (403) or size (413), OPTIONS requests, and GETs without `query`.
- Counted even when Apollo then rejects them: wrong `Content-Type`, parse errors, validation errors.

### Strict limits by operation

On top of the general limit, these root fields have their own limits. Each occurrence in a request counts once, so aliasing [`login`](#login) three times uses three. Strict limits are only counted when the general limit let the request through.

| Group | Root fields | Limit | Counted per |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sign-in | [`login`](#login), [`adminLogin`](#adminlogin) | 10 per 15 minutes per email or user; 100 per 15 minutes per IP | Email and signed-in user, plus IP at the higher limit |
| Registration | [`register`](#register) | 5 per minute per email or user; 30 per minute per IP | Email and signed-in user, plus IP at the higher limit |
| Token refresh | [`refreshToken`](#refreshtoken), [`adminRefreshToken`](#adminrefreshtoken) | 120 per minute | Signed-in user, or IP when no valid access token is sent |
| Asking for a reset code | [`forgotPassword`](#forgotpassword), [`adminForgotPassword`](#adminforgotpassword) | 3 per hour per email or user; 30 per hour per IP | Email and signed-in user, plus IP at the higher limit |
| Entering a reset code | [`resetPassword`](#resetpassword), [`adminResetPassword`](#adminresetpassword) | 10 per hour per email or user; 50 per hour per IP | Email and signed-in user, plus IP at the higher limit |
| Password change | [`changePassword`](#changepassword), [`adminChangePassword`](#adminchangepassword), [`deleteAccount`](#deleteaccount) | 5 per 15 minutes per user; 50 per 15 minutes per IP | Signed-in user, plus IP at the higher limit |
| Codes | [`verifyEmail`](#verifyemail), [`resendVerificationOtp`](#resendverificationotp), [`requestEmailChange`](#requestemailchange), [`confirmEmailChange`](#confirmemailchange), [`adminRequestEmailChange`](#adminrequestemailchange), [`adminConfirmEmailChange`](#adminconfirmemailchange) | 5 per 5 minutes per email or user; 50 per 5 minutes per IP | Email and signed-in user, plus IP at the higher limit |
| Uploads | [`uploadProfilePhoto`](#uploadprofilephoto), [`uploadProviderImages`](#uploadproviderimages), [`uploadServiceImages`](#uploadserviceimages), [`uploadProviderDocuments`](#uploadproviderdocuments), [`addProviderDocuments`](#addproviderdocuments) | 20 per minute | Signed-in user, or IP when not signed in |
| Messages | [`sendMessage`](#sendmessage), [`startConversation`](#startconversation) | 60 per minute | Signed-in user, or IP |
| Reports | [`createReport`](#createreport) | 10 per hour | Signed-in user, or IP |
| Blocking | [`blockUser`](#blockuser) | 20 per hour | Signed-in user, or IP |

For sign-in, registration, password resets, password changes and codes, every applicable identity is counted separately, and exceeding any one of them blocks the request:

- The email, when the request names one: an argument called `email`, or an `email` field inside an input-object argument, compared in lower case. [`login`](#login), [`register`](#register), [`forgotPassword`](#forgotpassword), [`resetPassword`](#resetpassword), [`verifyEmail`](#verifyemail) and [`resendVerificationOtp`](#resendverificationotp) name one. Email-change mutations don't.
- The user, when the request has a signed-in access token.
- The client IP, always, against the higher per-IP limit. It stops one address trying many accounts, while people who share a carrier IP don't lock each other out.

Asking for a reset code is limited to 3 per hour per email. Entering the code has its own limit of 10 per hour, so asking for codes never uses up the attempts to enter one.

### Limits inside operations

Some operations have limits of their own. They answer with a normal GraphQL error (HTTP 200), not a 429:

| Operations | Counted per | Limit | Error |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`register`](#register) | Email | 5 calls; the 6th within the hour blocks the email for 1 hour | `RATE_LIMITED` "Too many attempts. Please try again in 60 minutes." |
| [`login`](#login) | Email | 5 failed sign-ins within 5 minutes; the next attempt blocks for 15 minutes. A successful sign-in clears it. | `RATE_LIMITED` "Too many attempts. Please try again in 15 minutes." |
| [`verifyEmail`](#verifyemail), [`resetPassword`](#resetpassword) | Email | 5 wrong codes (or unknown email) within 5 minutes; the next attempt blocks for 10 minutes. Success clears it. | `RATE_LIMITED` "…in 10 minutes." |
| [`resendVerificationOtp`](#resendverificationotp) | Email | 3 calls within 5 minutes; the 4th blocks for 10 minutes | `RATE_LIMITED` "…in 10 minutes." |
| [`forgotPassword`](#forgotpassword) | Email | 3 calls within the hour; the 4th blocks for 1 hour. A successful [`resetPassword`](#resetpassword) clears it. | `RATE_LIMITED` "…in 60 minutes." |
| [`verifyBankAccount`](#verifybankaccount) and [`addBankAccount`](#addbankaccount), which verifies | User | 5 bank lookups in any rolling hour. Invalid input, an account already added, and re-checking an account verified in the last 15 minutes don't count. | `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` "Rate limit exceeded. You can verify up to 5 accounts per hour." with `extensions.resetIn` |
| [`adminBroadcastNotification`](#adminbroadcastnotification), [`superAdminBroadcastNotification`](#superadminbroadcastnotification) | Admin | 50 per 24 hours | `RATE_LIMITED` "Broadcast rate limit reached (50/day). Resets in Ns." |

- While a block is in force, the message uses the time left ("Please try again in N minutes").
- These `RATE_LIMITED` errors carry `extensions.resetIn` (seconds) and `extensions.blocked`.
- The email-based limits stop counting while Redis is unreachable. The bank-verification limit keeps applying.
- The admin sign-in and password mutations have no limits of their own, only the strict limits above.

### Rate limit headers

Every response to a request that reached the rate limiter (see [General limits](#general-limits)) has:

| Header | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | The limit of the bucket reported |
| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | Requests left in that bucket |
| `X-RateLimit-Reset` | Seconds until that bucket has room again |

The bucket reported is the one closest to its limit: fewest remaining, then the smaller limit. So a [`login`](#login) request reports the sign-in bucket (`10`, `9`, `900`), not the general one. A 429 reports the exceeded bucket that frees up last, and adds `Retry-After` with the same number of seconds as `X-RateLimit-Reset`.

### Client IP on Render

On Render (the server sees `RENDER=true`), traffic arrives through Cloudflare, and the client IP is the first address in the `True-Client-IP` header. Without that header, the server falls back to `X-Forwarded-For`: it takes the entry added by the outermost trusted proxy, which is the last entry with the default `TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT=1`. With neither header, the IP is `unknown`, and all such requests share one bucket.

Many Nigerian mobile users reach the internet through a carrier gateway that shares one public IP, and an office Wi-Fi does the same. Everyone behind that IP shares:

- the anonymous limit of 300 requests per minute (the server's `RATE_LIMIT_ANONYMOUS_PER_MINUTE` setting),
- the per-IP ceilings on the strict limits: 100 sign-ins per 15 minutes, 30 registrations per minute, 120 token refreshes per minute when no valid access token is sent, 30 reset-code requests and 50 reset-code attempts per hour, 50 password changes per 15 minutes, and 50 code attempts per 5 minutes.

The tighter per-email and per-user limits aren't shared. Still, sign users in as early as possible (signed-in general limits are per user), refresh tokens only when needed, and handle 429 on the sign-in, registration and refresh screens.

### Settings that change limits

These are server environment variables. The strict limits and the limits inside operations are fixed in code.

| Variable | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `RATE_LIMIT_READS_PER_MINUTE` | 300 | Signed-in queries per user per minute |
| `RATE_LIMIT_WRITES_PER_MINUTE` | 60 | Signed-in mutations per user per minute |
| `RATE_LIMIT_ANONYMOUS_PER_MINUTE` | 300 | Requests per IP per minute without a valid access token |
| `GRAPHQL_MAX_DEPTH` / `GRAPHQL_MAX_ROOT_FIELDS` / `GRAPHQL_MAX_ALIASES` | 10 / 20 / 30 | Complexity limits |
| `CLIENT_IP_HEADER` | `true-client-ip` on Render, otherwise none | Header holding the client IP |
| `TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT` | 1 | Proxies appending to `X-Forwarded-For` |
| `MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS` / `LOCKOUT_DURATION_MINUTES` | 5 / 30 | Account lockout |
| `RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS`, `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS` | n/a | No longer used |

A missing or invalid value falls back to the default.

## Conventions

### Pagination

List operations take `pagination: PaginationInput`. A few, such as [`providers`](#providers) and [`nearbyProviders`](#nearbyproviders), take it inside their input object instead.

```graphql
query BrowseServices($pagination: PaginationInput) {
  services(pagination: $pagination) {
    items {
      id
      name
      price
      createdAt
    }
    total
    page
    limit
    totalPages
    hasNextPage
    hasPreviousPage
  }
}
```

Variables:

```json
{ "pagination": { "page": 2, "limit": 20 } }
```

**Input.** `page` starts at 1 and `limit` is the page size. Both are optional.

- **Without `pagination`**, each operation uses its own default page size: 10 for most lists; 20 for [`services`](#services), [`myServices`](#myservices), [`nearbyServices`](#nearbyservices), [`myNotifications`](#mynotifications), [`myConversations`](#myconversations), [`myBlockedUsers`](#myblockedusers), [`myReports`](#myreports), [`reports`](#reports) and [`reportedConversationMessages`](#reportedconversationmessages); 50 for [`categories`](#categories) and [`conversationMessages`](#conversationmessages).
- **With `pagination`**, the values are normalised the same way for every operation before it runs, including when `pagination` sits inside an input object: a missing, zero or negative `page` becomes 1; a missing, zero or negative `limit` becomes that operation's default page size above; a `limit` above 100 becomes 100.
- Plain `limit` arguments, such as on [`topEarningProviders`](#topearningproviders), are capped at 100 the same way.

**Output.** Paginated types have `total`, `page`, `totalPages` and `hasNextPage`. Most also have `limit` and `hasPreviousPage`. `PaginatedPayments`, `PaginatedBlockedUsers`, `PaginatedWalletTransactions`, `PaginatedWithdrawals`, `PaginatedScheduledPayouts`, `PaginatedManagedUsers` and `PaginatedAuditLogs` don't. The list is usually `items`, but it's `reviews`, `favourites`, `disputes`, `conversations`, `messages` or `notifications` in those types. The nearby types add `radiusKm` and `searchLocation`.

### Dates and times

Dates are `String` fields in the schema. There are four forms:

| Form | Example | Where |
|---|---|---|
| ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC | `"2026-09-12T14:05:09.123Z"` | Almost every `...At` field: `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `paidAt`, `lastLoginAt`, `acceptedAt`, and so on |
| Date only, `YYYY-MM-DD` | `"2026-09-20"` | Inputs: `scheduledDate` when booking; `startDate` and `endDate` filters also accept full timestamps |
| Time only, `HH:mm`, 24-hour | `"14:00"` | `scheduledTime` on bookings, in and out |
| Unix time in seconds | `1789171200` | `SignedUploadParams.timestamp`, JWT `iat`/`exp` |

Bookings:

- You send `scheduledDate: "2026-09-20"` and `scheduledTime: "14:00"`.
- `Booking.scheduledDate` comes back as midnight UTC of that day (`"2026-09-20T00:00:00.000Z"`); take the first 10 characters. `scheduledTime` comes back as sent.
- The server reads `scheduledDate` and `scheduledTime` as Lagos time (Africa/Lagos, UTC+1, no daylight saving) for the 2-hour minimum, the 30-day maximum and the 24-hour cancellation window (`INVALID_BOOKING_TIME`).
- `scheduledDate` must be a real `YYYY-MM-DD` date and `scheduledTime` a 24-hour `HH:mm` from `00:00` to `23:59`; anything else is refused with `INVALID_BOOKING_TIME`.
- Timestamps nested inside results, such as a booking's `provider.createdAt`, are ISO strings like every other timestamp.

### Money

- **Every amount in the GraphQL API is in naira**, as a `Float`: `15000.5` means ₦15,000.50. There are no kobo fields in the schema.
- Amounts in results: `Service.price`; `Booking.servicePrice`, `commission` and `totalAmount`; `Payment.amount`, `commission`, `providerPayout` and `refundAmount`; `Wallet.balance` and `pendingBalance`; `WalletTransaction.amount` and `balanceAfter`; `Withdrawal.amount`, `fee` and `netAmount`; payout amounts; analytics totals.
- Amounts in inputs are naira too: service `price` (at most 2 decimal places, otherwise `INVALID_INPUT` "Price can have at most 2 decimal places"), withdrawal `amount`, admin wallet adjustments and dispute `refundAmount`.
- The customer pays the service price. Commission comes out of it; it isn't added on top, so `Booking.totalAmount` equals `servicePrice`.
- Wallets, withdrawals, payouts and Paystack use whole kobo internally, so amounts are exact to the kobo. Show two decimals.
- `commissionRate` fields (`PlatformSettings`, `ProviderEarnings`, `PaymentStats`) are percentages: `7` means 7%.

### Text is stored as plain text

The server removes HTML from text before saving it: names, addresses, descriptions, reviews, review responses and chat messages. It trims spaces at the ends, deletes tags (and the contents of `<script>` and `<style>`), and keeps `<` and `>` that aren't part of a tag escaped as `&lt;` and `&gt;`. Everything else, including `&`, quotes and apostrophes, is stored as typed.

| You send | Stored and returned |
|---|---|
| `Tom & Jerry's <b>best</b> "deal"` | `Tom & Jerry's best "deal"` |
| `<script>alert(1)</script>Hello` | `Hello` |
| `2 < 5 > 1` | `2 &lt; 5 &gt; 1` |
| `<p>Clean <i>home</i></p><img src=x onerror=alert(1)>` | `Clean home` |
| `<a href="https://example.com">link</a>` | `link` |
| `R&B and 100% "fresh"` | `R&B and 100% "fresh"` |
| `  padded  ` | `padded` |

In the app:

- **Display:** show text as text. Decode `&lt;` and `&gt;` if you want the characters back; never render user text as HTML.
- **Older records** saved before this rule may still contain `&amp;`, `&lt;` or `&gt;`. Decoding those three covers both.
- **Lengths** are measured after tags are removed.

### Content filter

Text shown to other people is screened for blocked language and for contact or bank details.

| Where | Blocked language | Contact details |
|---|---|---|
| Chat messages ([`sendMessage`](#sendmessage), and the first message of [`startConversation`](#startconversation)) | Replaced with `*` in the saved message, so everyone sees it masked. The original is reported to admins. | Allowed. A message with bank details (a long number plus a bank word such as "account", "GTBank", "OPay") is delivered unchanged and reported to admins. |
| Reviews and review responses | Rejected: `INAPPROPRIATE_CONTENT` | Rejected: `CONTACT_DETAILS_NOT_ALLOWED` |
| Service name and description | Rejected | Rejected |
| Business name and description | Rejected | Rejected |
| First and last name ([`register`](#register), [`updateProfile`](#updateprofile)) | Rejected | Rejected |

**Blocked language** is a built-in list of strong profanity and slurs, plus any words in the server's `CONTENT_FILTER_TERMS`. Matching:

- whole words only, in any case, with an optional plural ending,
- catches look-alike characters (`4`/`@` for a, `3` for e, `1`/`!` for i, `0` for o, `5`/`$` for s, `7` for t) and stretched letters,
- skips a match that is half digits or more, so codes like `SH17` pass.

**Contact details** are:

- email addresses,
- Nigerian mobile numbers, with or without `+234`, spaces or dashes,
- account-style numbers: 10 or more digits in a row, or digit groups such as `0123 456 789` adding up to 10 or more.

Dates, times and prices don't match.

| Text | Chat message is saved as | In a review |
|---|---|---|
| `This is shit work` | `This is **** work` | `INAPPROPRIATE_CONTENT` "Your review contains language that isn't allowed on Easykonnet" |
| `Call me on 0803 123 4567` | unchanged | `CONTACT_DETAILS_NOT_ALLOWED` "Your review can't include phone numbers, email addresses or account numbers. You can share contact details in chat once a booking is made." |
| `Pay to GTBank 0123456789` | unchanged, reported to admins | `CONTACT_DETAILS_NOT_ALLOWED` |
| `Booked for 12/09 at 14:00, price 5000` | unchanged | accepted |

### Community terms

- [`termsStatus`](#termsstatus) returns `currentVersion` (the server's `TERMS_VERSION`, default `2026-09`), `acceptedVersion`, `acceptedAt` and `mustAccept`.
- [`acceptTerms`](#acceptterms) needs the current version; any other version gets `TERMS_VERSION_OUTDATED`.

```graphql
query TermsStatus {
  termsStatus {
    currentVersion
    acceptedVersion
    mustAccept
  }
}
```

```graphql
mutation AcceptTerms($version: String!) {
  acceptTerms(version: $version) {
    currentVersion
    acceptedVersion
    acceptedAt
    mustAccept
  }
}
```

Variables:

```json
{ "version": "2026-09" }
```

Acceptance is optional by default. When the server sets `REQUIRE_TERMS_ACCEPTANCE=true`, these fail with `TERMS_NOT_ACCEPTED` "Please accept the community terms before posting" until the current version is accepted:

- [`sendMessage`](#sendmessage)
- [`startConversation`](#startconversation) when it has an `initialMessage`
- [`createReview`](#createreview)
- [`updateReview`](#updatereview) when it changes `comment`
- [`respondToReview`](#respondtoreview)
- [`createService`](#createservice)
- [`updateService`](#updateservice) when it changes the name, description or images

Show the terms whenever `mustAccept` is true, so turning the setting on doesn't break anything. The version changes when the terms change, and then everyone must accept again.

### Enums and JSON strings

- Enum values travel as their names in JSON strings, for example `"role": "SERVICE_PROVIDER"`. Send them as strings in variables. Written inline in the query text, they have no quotes: `switchActiveRole(targetRole: SERVICE_USER)`.
- An unknown enum value gets 400 `BAD_USER_INPUT` in variables, or `GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED` inline.
- Handle values you don't know, because enums can grow.
- Some fields hold JSON encoded as a string; parse it yourself: `Notification.metadata`, `NotificationStats.byType`, and the `metadataJson` input of the broadcast mutations.

## File uploads

### What works today

Files either go through the backend as base64 inside a GraphQL mutation, which uploads and saves them in one step, or go straight from the device to Cloudinary with signed parameters (see [Signed direct uploads](#signed-direct-uploads)).

| What | Mutation | Who | Saves to |
|---|---|---|---|
| Profile photo | [`uploadProfilePhoto`](#uploadprofilephoto) | Any signed-in user | `User.profilePhoto`, replacing and deleting the old photo |
| Provider gallery | [`uploadProviderImages`](#uploadproviderimages) | A provider, for their own profile | `ServiceProviderProfile.images` |
| Service images | [`uploadServiceImages`](#uploadserviceimages) | The provider who owns the service | `Service.images` |
| Verification documents | [`uploadProviderDocuments`](#uploadproviderdocuments), or upload directly and save with [`addProviderDocuments`](#addproviderdocuments) | A provider, for their own profile | `ServiceProviderProfile.documents` |
| Dispute evidence | Direct upload with [`getEvidenceUploadParams`](#getevidenceuploadparams) | Any signed-in user | URLs passed to [`createDispute`](#createdispute) / [`addDisputeEvidence`](#adddisputeevidence) |

### Upload mutations

Each file is a `FileUploadInput`:

- `base64Data`: raw base64, or a data URI (`data:image/jpeg;base64,...`).
- `filename`: its extension decides whether the type is allowed.

```graphql
mutation UploadProfilePhoto($file: FileUploadInput!) {
  uploadProfilePhoto(file: $file) {
    success
    url
    publicId
    message
  }
}
```

Variables:

```json
{ "file": { "base64Data": "data:image/jpeg;base64,/9j/4AAQSkZJRgABAQAAAQABAAD", "filename": "avatar.jpg" } }
```

- [`uploadProfilePhoto`](#uploadprofilephoto) returns `success`, `url`, `publicId` and `message`.
- The multi-file mutations take `files: [FileUploadInput!]!` and return `success`, `urls` and `message`. Every file is checked before any is uploaded; if an upload or the save fails, the files that request already uploaded are deleted.
- [`uploadProviderDocuments`](#uploadproviderdocuments) returns download links that expire after 30 minutes, not permanent URLs (see [Ownership and privacy](#ownership-and-privacy)).

### Types, sizes and counts

| Kind | Extensions | Max size per file | Max files |
|---|---|---|---|
| Profile photo | jpg, jpeg, png, webp | 5 MB | 1. Cropped to 400×400 around the face. |
| Provider gallery and service images | jpg, jpeg, png, webp, gif | 10 MB | 10 in total on the service or gallery, existing images included |
| Provider documents | jpg, jpeg, png, pdf, doc, docx | 15 MB | 5 in total |

The size is estimated from the base64 length. Errors:

| Code | Message |
|---|---|
| `INVALID_FILE_FORMAT` | Invalid file format. Allowed formats for {kind}: {list} |
| `FILE_TOO_LARGE` | File size exceeds maximum allowed (N MB) |
| `MAX_IMAGES_EXCEEDED` | Maximum 10 images allowed per service. You have N and are trying to add M. (the gallery message starts "Maximum 10 images allowed.") |
| `MAX_DOCUMENTS_EXCEEDED` | Maximum 5 documents allowed. You have N and are trying to add M. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Service not found |
| `PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND` | Provider profile not found |
| `TERMS_NOT_ACCEPTED` | Please accept the community terms before posting (service images, when terms acceptance is required) |
| `FORBIDDEN` | You can only upload images to your own services |
| `UPLOAD_FAILED` | Cloudinary's own error text; don't show it |
