Uploads also have a strict limit of 20 per minute per user. Each mutation counts once, however many files it carries.

### Upload request size

A request that uploads files can be up to 20 MB (see [Request size](#request-size)). Base64 is a third larger than the file, so one request can carry about **15 MB** of file data in total. The per-file limits in the table above apply within that.

- Several large files in one request can still go over 20 MB and get `413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, so send large files one per request.
- Resizing images first still makes uploads much faster on mobile data. About 1280 px on the long side at JPEG quality 0.7 is plenty for listings.

```ts
const approxBytes = Math.ceil((base64.length * 3) / 4);
if (approxBytes > 15_000_000) {
  // too big for one request: send the files separately or compress them
}
```

### Signed direct uploads

[`getProfileUploadParams`](#getprofileuploadparams) (any signed-in user), [`getServiceUploadParams`](#getserviceuploadparams) and [`getDocumentUploadParams`](#getdocumentuploadparams) (providers), and [`getEvidenceUploadParams`](#getevidenceuploadparams) (any signed-in user) return parameters for uploading **one file** straight to Cloudinary, into these folders:

- `easykonect/profiles`
- `easykonect/services`
- `easykonect/documents`
- `easykonect/evidence`

```graphql
query ProfileUploadParams {
  getProfileUploadParams {
    uploadUrl
    signature
    timestamp
    apiKey
    folder
    publicId
    allowedFormats
    type
    overwrite
  }
}
```

1. Fetch new parameters for each file, bypassing any client cache. They expire after an hour.
2. POST the file as `multipart/form-data` to `uploadUrl` with `file`, `api_key`, `timestamp`, `signature`, `folder`, `public_id`, `allowed_formats`, `type` and `overwrite` (the text `false`), exactly as returned. Cloudinary rejects changed fields and disallowed formats.
3. Save the `secure_url` Cloudinary returns: the profile photo with [`updateProfile`](#updateprofile), service images with [`createService`](#createservice) / [`updateService`](#updateservice), documents with [`addProviderDocuments`](#addproviderdocuments), and evidence with [`createDispute`](#createdispute) / [`addDisputeEvidence`](#adddisputeevidence).

Documents upload as private files. Provider gallery images can only be added with [`uploadProviderImages`](#uploadproviderimages).

### Fields that take a URL

| Field | What the server checks |
|---|---|
| `profilePhoto` in [`updateProfile`](#updateprofile) | Must be an `http` or `https` URL of at most 2,048 characters (`INVALID_URL`). Any host is accepted. |
| `profilePhoto` in [`updateProviderProfile`](#updateproviderprofile) | Must be a valid URL (`INVALID_URL`); empty or `null` removes the photo |
| `images` in [`createService`](#createservice) and [`updateService`](#updateservice) | At most 10, each an `https` image URL in the backend's own Cloudinary cloud (`MAX_IMAGES_EXCEEDED`, `INVALID_IMAGE_URL`). Changing the images, name or description of a live (`ACTIVE`) listing reports it to admins for review; the listing stays live. |
| `documentUrls` in [`addProviderDocuments`](#addproviderdocuments) | Private files you uploaded to the documents folder with [`getDocumentUploadParams`](#getdocumentuploadparams) (`INVALID_DOCUMENT_URL`) |
| `evidence` in [`createDispute`](#createdispute) and [`addDisputeEvidence`](#adddisputeevidence) | Nothing: any strings. [`addDisputeEvidence`](#adddisputeevidence) allows 10 in total (`MAX_EVIDENCE_EXCEEDED` "Maximum 10 evidence files allowed"). |
| `attachments` in [`sendMessage`](#sendmessage) | Nothing: any strings |

Send only URLs returned by the upload mutations, or the `secure_url` Cloudinary returns from a direct upload.

### Ownership and privacy

- Uploads always attach to the caller's own records. [`uploadServiceImages`](#uploadserviceimages) checks that the caller's provider profile owns the service.
- Each uploaded file is named `<userId>_<timestamp>_<random>`. When an image or document is removed, or a profile photo replaced, the backend deletes the Cloudinary file only if it's in the backend's own Cloudinary account and that user uploaded it. Other URLs are just removed from the record.
- Verification documents are stored privately. `ServiceProviderProfile.documents` goes only to the provider and to admins, as download links that expire after 30 minutes (older documents are returned as stored); everyone else gets `[]`. Don't store the links; fetch the profile again when you need them.

### Removing files

| Mutation | Takes | Errors |
|---|---|---|
| [`removeProfilePhoto`](#removeprofilephoto) | nothing | `NO_PHOTO` "No profile photo to remove" |
| [`removeProviderImage`](#removeproviderimage) | `imageUrl` | `IMAGE_NOT_FOUND` "Image not found in provider gallery" |
| [`removeServiceImage`](#removeserviceimage) | `serviceId`, `imageUrl` | `IMAGE_NOT_FOUND` "Image not found in service", `FORBIDDEN` |
| [`removeProviderDocument`](#removeproviderdocument) | `documentUrl` | `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` "Document not found" |

The URL must match the stored one exactly, except that [`removeProviderDocument`](#removeproviderdocument) also accepts a download link returned in `documents`, even an expired one.

## Push notifications

### Setting up OneSignal in the app

- **Which app.** The backend sends through the OneSignal app set in `ONESIGNAL_APP_ID` on the Render service. That App ID isn't in the repository; get it from the backend owner and use the same one in the mobile app.
- **iOS.** Delivery on iOS also needs APNs credentials added to that OneSignal app.
- **Configuration.** Pushes only go out when the server has both `ONESIGNAL_APP_ID` and `ONESIGNAL_REST_API_KEY`. Otherwise sending is skipped silently.

With `react-native-onesignal` 5.x:

```ts
import { OneSignal } from 'react-native-onesignal';

OneSignal.initialize(ONESIGNAL_APP_ID); // the same app as the backend's ONESIGNAL_APP_ID

async function afterSignIn(userId: string) {
  await OneSignal.Notifications.requestPermission(true);
  OneSignal.login(userId); // link this device to the Easykonnet user ID
  const subscriptionId = await OneSignal.User.pushSubscription.getIdAsync();
  if (subscriptionId) await registerPushToken(subscriptionId); // calls the mutation below
}

OneSignal.User.pushSubscription.addEventListener('change', ({ current }) => {
  if (current.id) registerPushToken(current.id);
});

OneSignal.Notifications.addEventListener('click', (event) => {
  openFromPush(event.notification.additionalData); // see "Data payload for deep links"
});
```

- **The ID to register.** The backend calls the ID a "player ID". In OneSignal's current SDKs it's the push subscription ID.
- **`OneSignal.login(userId)`.** When the server uses a new-style OneSignal App API key (`os_v2_...`), the backend can't link the device to the user itself, and relies on this call. With an older REST API key, the backend also sets the link. Call it either way.

### Registering and unregistering the device

```graphql
mutation RegisterDevice($playerId: String!) {
  registerPushToken(playerId: $playerId) {
    success
    message
    pushEnabled
  }
}
```

Variables:

```json
{ "playerId": "5f1e2d3c-4b5a-4978-8a9b-0c1d2e3f4a5b" }
```

- **Registering.** [`registerPushToken`](#registerpushtoken) adds this device (the ID is trimmed) and switches `pushEnabled` on, unless the user switched push off with [`updatePushPreference`](#updatepushpreference) or [`togglePushNotifications`](#togglepushnotifications); that choice is kept. [`enablePushNotifications`](#enablepushnotifications) does the same but always switches push on. An empty ID gets `VALIDATION_ERROR` "Player ID is required". Call it after every sign-in, and whenever the subscription ID changes.
- **Several devices per account.** Each account keeps up to 10 devices, and every push goes to all of them. A device ID belongs to one account at a time: registering it for another user removes it from the previous one.
- **Unregistering.** Call [`unregisterPushToken`](#unregisterpushtoken) with this device's `playerId` **before** [`logout`](#logout), while the access token still works, then call `OneSignal.logout()`. Only that device is removed. Without `playerId`, or with [`disablePushNotifications`](#disablepushnotifications), every device is removed and `pushEnabled` turns off. Neither counts as the user switching push off. [`deactivateMyAccount`](#deactivatemyaccount) unregisters too.
- **Muting.** [`updatePushPreference`](#updatepushpreference) and [`togglePushNotifications`](#togglepushnotifications) switch `pushEnabled` without touching the stored devices. Switching off is remembered when a device is registered later. Pushes go out only when `pushEnabled` is true and a device is stored.
- **Status.** [`myPushStatus`](#mypushstatus) returns `pushEnabled`, `hasDeviceRegistered` and `playerId`, which is the most recently registered device.

```graphql
query PushStatus {
  myPushStatus {
    pushEnabled
    hasDeviceRegistered
    playerId
  }
}
```

```graphql
mutation UnregisterDevice($playerId: String) {
  unregisterPushToken(playerId: $playerId) {
    success
    pushEnabled
  }
}
```

Variables:

```json
{ "playerId": "5f1e2d3c-4b5a-4978-8a9b-0c1d2e3f4a5b" }
```

The `notify*` switches in [`mySettings`](#mysettings) / [`updateMySettings`](#updatemysettings) decide which pushes go out:

| Switch | Pushes it controls |
|---|---|
| `notifyMessages` | Chat messages |
| `notifyBookingUpdates` | Booking pushes |
| `notifyReviews` | New reviews and replies to reviews |
| `notifyDisputeUpdates` | Dispute pushes |
| `notifyProviderVerification` | Verification decisions, and service approvals and rejections |

Payments, refunds, withdrawals, account status, service suspensions and broadcasts always go out. In-app notifications are always created. `Notification.isPushed` and `pushedAt` are set when a push goes out for a chat message, a dispute or a broadcast notification.

### When pushes are sent

Pushes carry no URL or buttons.

| Event | Recipient | Title | `data` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Customer requests a booking | Provider | New Booking Request | `type: "BOOKING"`, `bookingId`, `action: "new"` |
| Provider accepts a booking | Customer | Booking Accepted! 🎉 | `type: "BOOKING"`, `bookingId`, `action: "accepted"` |
| Provider rejects a booking | Customer | Booking Update | `type: "BOOKING"`, `bookingId`, `action: "rejected"` |
| Provider marks the job complete | Customer | Booking Completed | `type: "BOOKING"`, `bookingId`, `action: "completed"` |
| Customer confirms delivery | Provider | Delivery Confirmed | `type: "BOOKING"`, `bookingId`, `action: "confirmed"` |
| Customer cancels | Provider | Booking Cancelled | `type: "BOOKING"`, `bookingId`, `action: "cancelled"` |
| Admin cancels | Customer and provider | Booking Cancelled | `type: "BOOKING"`, `bookingId`, `action: "cancelled"` |
| Cancellation refunds a paid booking to the wallet | Customer | Refund added to your wallet | `type: "REFUND_PROCESSED"`, `bookingId` |
| Checkout or wallet payment succeeds | Customer | Payment Successful | `type: "PAYMENT_RECEIVED"`, `bookingId`, `paymentId` |
| Checkout or wallet payment succeeds | Provider | Payment Secured | `type: "PAYMENT_RECEIVED"`, `bookingId`, `paymentId` |
| Checkout payment fails | Customer | Payment Failed | `type: "PAYMENT_FAILED"`, `bookingId`, `paymentId` |
| A payment arrives for a booking that was already paid or can't be paid, and goes to the wallet | Customer | Payment added to your wallet | `type: "REFUND_PROCESSED"`, `bookingId`, `paymentId` |
| Super admin refunds a payment | Customer | Refund added to your wallet | `type: "REFUND_PROCESSED"`, `bookingId`, `paymentId` |
| Super admin refunds a payment | Provider | Booking refunded | `type: "REFUND_PROCESSED"`, `bookingId`, `paymentId` |
| Withdrawal paid out | Provider | Withdrawal Successful | `type: "PAYMENT_RECEIVED"`, `withdrawalId` |
| Withdrawal rejected | Provider | Withdrawal Rejected | `type: "PAYMENT_FAILED"`, `withdrawalId` |
| Withdrawal failed after retries | Provider | Withdrawal Failed | `type: "PAYMENT_FAILED"`, `withdrawalId` |
| Bank returned the transfer | Provider | Withdrawal Returned | `type: "PAYMENT_FAILED"`, `withdrawalId` |
| Dispute opened | The other party | Dispute opened | `type: "DISPUTE_OPENED"`, `disputeId`, `bookingId` |
| Admin takes the dispute under review | Customer and provider | Dispute under review | `type: "DISPUTE_UPDATED"`, `disputeId`, `bookingId` |
| Dispute resolved | Customer and provider | Dispute resolved | `type: "DISPUTE_RESOLVED"`, `disputeId`, `bookingId` |
| New chat message | Other participants | New message from {name} (the text is "Sent an attachment" when there's no text) | `type: "MESSAGE"`, `conversationId` |
| New review | Provider | New Review Received ⭐ | `type: "REVIEW"`, `reviewId` |
| Provider replies to a review | Customer who wrote it | Provider Responded to Your Review | `type: "REVIEW"`, `reviewId` |
| Provider verification approved or rejected | Provider | Verification Approved! 🎉 / Verification Update | `type: "VERIFICATION"`, `status: "approved"` or `"rejected"` |
| Service approved, rejected, suspended or reinstated | Provider | Service Approved / Service Rejected / Service Suspended / Service Reinstated | `type: "SERVICE"`, `serviceId`, `action: "approved"`, `"rejected"`, `"suspended"` or `"reinstated"` |
| Account suspended | User | Account Suspended | `type: "ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED"`, `reason` |
| Suspension or deactivation lifted by an admin | User | Account Reactivated | `type: "ACCOUNT_ACTIVATED"` |
| Account banned | User | Account Banned | `type: "ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED"`, `reason`, `bannedUntil` (ISO string, or `null` for a permanent ban) |
| Ban lifted | User | Account Unbanned | `type: "ACCOUNT_ACTIVATED"` |
| Account restricted | User | Account Restricted | `type: "ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED"`, `reason`, `restrictedUntil` |
| Restriction removed | User | Restriction Removed | `type: "ACCOUNT_ACTIVATED"` |
| Admin or super admin broadcast | Chosen active users who aren't banned | Broadcast title | `type: "SYSTEM_ANNOUNCEMENT"` plus the keys of `metadataJson` (a `type` key there doesn't replace it) |

No push is sent for:

- the provider starting the job (the in-app notification and socket event only),
- [`sendSystemAnnouncement`](#sendsystemannouncement) (in-app notification and `notification:new` only),
- alerts to admins about new or reopened disputes and new withdrawal requests (in-app only),
- a skipped scheduled payout (in-app only).

Most events also create an in-app notification ([`myNotifications`](#mynotifications)).

### Data payload for deep links

The `data` object arrives as OneSignal's `additionalData`. Route by `type`, and use field presence where one `type` covers two cases:

```ts
type PushData =
  | { type: 'BOOKING'; bookingId: string; action: 'new' | 'accepted' | 'rejected' | 'completed' | 'confirmed' | 'cancelled' }
  | { type: 'MESSAGE'; conversationId: string }
  | { type: 'REVIEW'; reviewId?: string }
  | { type: 'VERIFICATION'; status: 'approved' | 'rejected' }
  | { type: 'SERVICE'; serviceId: string; action: 'approved' | 'rejected' | 'suspended' | 'reinstated' }
  | { type: 'PAYMENT_RECEIVED' | 'PAYMENT_FAILED'; bookingId?: string; paymentId?: string; withdrawalId?: string }
  | { type: 'REFUND_PROCESSED'; bookingId: string; paymentId?: string }
  | { type: 'DISPUTE_OPENED' | 'DISPUTE_UPDATED' | 'DISPUTE_RESOLVED'; disputeId: string; bookingId: string }
  | { type: 'ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED'; reason: string; bannedUntil?: string | null; restrictedUntil?: string }
  | { type: 'ACCOUNT_ACTIVATED' }
  | { type: 'SYSTEM_ANNOUNCEMENT'; [key: string]: unknown };

function openFromPush(data?: Record<string, unknown>) {
  const push = data as PushData | undefined;
  switch (push?.type) {
    case 'BOOKING': return navigate('Booking', { id: push.bookingId });
    case 'MESSAGE': return navigate('Chat', { conversationId: push.conversationId });
    case 'PAYMENT_RECEIVED':
    case 'PAYMENT_FAILED':
      return push.withdrawalId
        ? navigate('Withdrawal', { id: push.withdrawalId })
        : navigate('Booking', { id: push.bookingId });
    case 'REFUND_PROCESSED': return navigate('Wallet');
    case 'REVIEW': return navigate('Reviews');
    case 'VERIFICATION': return navigate('ProviderVerification');
    case 'SERVICE': return navigate('Service', { id: push.serviceId });
    case 'DISPUTE_OPENED':
    case 'DISPUTE_UPDATED':
    case 'DISPUTE_RESOLVED': return navigate('Dispute', { id: push.disputeId });
    case 'ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED':
    case 'ACCOUNT_ACTIVATED': return navigate('AccountStatus');
    default: return navigate('Notifications');
  }
}
```

Types to expect:

- `ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED` covers suspensions (only `reason`), bans (`bannedUntil` present) and restrictions (`restrictedUntil` present).
- Payment and withdrawal pushes share `PAYMENT_RECEIVED` and `PAYMENT_FAILED`; `withdrawalId` tells them apart.
- An account can be signed out by the time a push is opened (for example after a ban), so load the target screen through the normal auth flow.

## REST endpoints

| Route | Methods | For |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/graphql` | POST, GET, OPTIONS | Everything the apps do |
| `/api/health` | GET | Health check: is the server up |
| `/api/payments/paystack/callback` | GET | Paystack's browser redirect after checkout; returns the customer to the app |
| `/api/webhooks/paystack` | POST (GET answers a status message) | Paystack's servers only. The app must never call it. |
| `/api/socket` | GET, POST | Information only; Socket.IO itself is at `/socket.io/` |

### GraphQL: /api/graphql

| Method | Request | Responses |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | JSON body, `Content-Type: application/json`, optional `Authorization` | 200 with `data`/`errors`; 400, 403, 413 and 429 as in [HTTP-level errors](#http-level-errors) |
| `GET` with `query` | Search parameters, `apollo-require-preflight: true`, no `Content-Type` | Same as POST, plus 405 for mutations |
| `GET` without `query` | n/a | 400 `BAD_REQUEST` (see [HTTP methods](#http-methods)) |
| `OPTIONS` | Preflight | 204 with the CORS headers |

Checks run in this order:

1. IP blocklist (403)
2. Declared body size over 20 MB (413, POST only)
3. A body that isn't valid JSON (400, POST only)
4. Complexity (400)
5. A body over 1 MB without an upload mutation (413, POST only)
6. Rate limits (429)
7. Apollo: request format, parsing, validation, then the operation

### Health check: /api/health

`GET /api/health` answers `200` with `{"status":"ok"}`. It doesn't touch the database, Redis or GraphQL, and no rate limit applies. Render's health check uses it (`healthCheckPath` in `render.yaml`). The app can call it to wake a sleeping server before showing the sign-in screen.

### Paystack return page: /api/payments/paystack/callback

**What it's for.** Paystack's hosted checkout can only redirect a browser to an `http(s)` address, not to `easykonnect://`. So when the app passes `returnDeepLink` to [`initializePayment`](#initializepayment), the backend tells Paystack to send the customer here. This page verifies the payment and returns the customer to the app.

```graphql
mutation StartCheckout($input: InitializePaymentInput!) {
  initializePayment(input: $input) {
    authorizationUrl
    reference
  }
}
```

Variables:

```json
{ "input": { "bookingId": "64f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1", "returnDeepLink": "easykonnect://payment-callback" } }
```

**Allowed return links.** `returnDeepLink` must use one of the app's URL schemes (server setting `APP_URL_SCHEMES`, default `easykonnect` and `easykonnet`), or be an `http(s)` URL on the server's `FRONTEND_URL` or `BACKEND_URL` origin. Anything else gets `INVALID_RETURN_LINK` "returnDeepLink must be a link into the Easykonnet app".

**Where Paystack sends the customer:**

- With `returnDeepLink`: here, `<BACKEND_URL>/api/payments/paystack/callback`. If the server has no `BACKEND_URL`, the base is `FRONTEND_URL`, and the customer lands on the website.
- Without it: the `callbackUrl` you pass (web flow), which must be a page on the `FRONTEND_URL` or `BACKEND_URL` origin (otherwise `INVALID_RETURN_LINK` "callbackUrl must be a page on the Easykonnet website"), or `<FRONTEND_URL>/payment/callback`.

**Request.** `GET /api/payments/paystack/callback?reference=<ref>` (Paystack may send `trxref` instead; either works). The reference must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,100}$`. No authentication.

**What it does:**

1. Verifies the payment with Paystack and applies it to the booking if the webhook hasn't yet. This is the same work as [`verifyPayment`](#verifypayment), without the ownership check.
2. Reads `returnDeepLink` back from the Paystack transaction's metadata, and keeps it only if it's still an allowed link.
3. Answers with a small HTML page that immediately navigates to the target, with an "Open the app" button as a fallback.

**Responses:**

| Status | When | Page navigates to |
|---|---|---|
| 200 `text/html` | Valid reference, allowed deep link recovered | `<returnDeepLink>?reference=<ref>&status=success` or `&status=failed`. If the link already has a query string, the parameters are appended with `&`. |
| 200 `text/html` | Valid reference, no allowed link recovered (Paystack unreachable, web checkout) | `<FRONTEND_URL>/payment/callback?reference=<ref>` (no `status`) |
| 400 `text/html` | Missing or malformed reference | `<FRONTEND_URL>/payment/callback` |

`status=success` means the verification reported the payment as verified. `status=failed` covers everything else: declined, abandoned, still pending (for example a bank transfer that hasn't landed), or verification itself failing. The app should:

- register its URL scheme and handle `easykonnect://payment-callback?reference=...&status=...`,
- treat `status` as a hint, and confirm with [`verifyPayment`](#verifypayment) or [`paymentByBooking`](#paymentbybooking) before showing the result,
- handle the customer closing the browser without being redirected, by checking the payment when the app comes back to the foreground.

### Paystack webhook: /api/webhooks/paystack

Paystack's servers call this route to report charges, transfers and refunds. **The app must never call it.** Requests must carry an `x-paystack-signature` header: an HMAC-SHA512 of the raw body, keyed with the Paystack secret key, which only the server holds.

| Method | Responses |
|---|---|
| `POST` | 400 `{"error":"Missing signature"}`; 401 `{"error":"Invalid signature"}`; 200 `{"received":true}`, `{"received":true,"duplicate":true}` (already processed) or `{"received":true,"flagged":"<CODE>"}` (an event that can't be applied and won't succeed on a retry; for a charge, admins are alerted); 500 `{"received":false}` (Paystack retries) |
| `GET` | 200 `{"status":"ok","message":"Paystack webhook endpoint is active","supportedEvents":["charge.success","charge.failed","transfer.success","transfer.failed","refund.processed"]}` |

- **Events handled:** `charge.success`, `charge.failed`, `transfer.success`, `transfer.failed` and `transfer.reversed`. `refund.processed` and `refund.failed` are only logged.
- **Limits:** the route has no rate limits and no CORS headers.
- **Effect on the app:** payment and withdrawal changes it makes reach the app through pushes, in-app notifications and socket events.

### Socket information: /api/socket

| Method | Response |
|---|---|
| `GET` | 200 `{"status":"ok","message":"WebSocket server is available","info":{"connection":"Use socket.io-client to connect","endpoint":"/socket.io/","transport":["websocket","polling"]},"note":"WebSocket connections are served by the custom server (npm run start:ws), not by this route"}` |
| `POST` | 400 `{"error":"WebSocket upgrade not supported via API routes","solution":"Connect with socket.io-client to /socket.io/ on the custom server (npm run start:ws)","alternatives":[...]}` |

This route doesn't accept socket connections. The Socket.IO server runs on the same host at Socket.IO's default path, `/socket.io/`, when the backend is started with its custom server (as on Render). Connect with `socket.io-client` to the base URL (`https://backend-ehtm.onrender.com`) and pass the access token as `auth: { token }` or an `Authorization: Bearer` header. The realtime events chapter covers the events.

# Part 2: Realtime and guides

## Realtime (Socket.IO)

The backend sends live updates over Socket.IO: chat messages, typing indicators, read receipts, presence, booking changes, and every in-app notification as it's created. Other changes, such as payments, refunds, payment releases, disputes, withdrawals and verification results, have no event of their own: when they create an in-app notification it arrives as `notification:new`, and otherwise you fetch them. Use the socket to update screens faster, never as the only source of truth.

### Connecting

| | |
|---|---|
| URL | `https://backend-ehtm.onrender.com` (the same host as `/api/graphql`) |
| Path | `/socket.io/`, the Socket.IO default. `/api/socket` only returns an information page and doesn't accept connections. |
| Client library | `socket.io-client` 4.x (the server runs Socket.IO 4.8) |
| Transports | `websocket` and `polling` are both accepted. Use `transports: ['websocket']` in the mobile app. |
| Keep-alive | The server pings every 25 seconds and drops a client that doesn't answer within 60 seconds. |
| Sign-in | The access token in `auth.token`, or an `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` header. A refresh token is refused. |
| Heartbeat | Emit `heartbeat` every 60 seconds while the app is in the foreground (see `heartbeat` below). |

```js
import { io } from 'socket.io-client';

const socket = io('https://backend-ehtm.onrender.com', {
  transports: ['websocket'],
  // A function, so every reconnection sends the current access token
  auth: (cb) => cb({ token: tokenStore.accessToken }),
});

let heartbeat;

socket.on('connect', () => {
  // The server handles events as soon as `connect` fires. Rooms belong to one
  // connection, so join the open chat again after every reconnect.
  if (openConversationId) {
    socket.emit('conversation:join', { conversationId: openConversationId });
  }
  clearInterval(heartbeat);
  heartbeat = setInterval(() => socket.emit('heartbeat'), 60 * 1000);
});

socket.on('disconnect', () => clearInterval(heartbeat));

socket.on('connect_error', async (err) => {
  if (err.message === 'Invalid token' || err.message === 'Authentication failed') {
    const refreshed = await tokenStore.refresh(); // the refreshToken mutation
    if (refreshed) socket.connect();
    else signOut();
  }
});

// The server ended this connection's session; it disconnects the socket next
socket.on('session:ended', async () => {
  const refreshed = await tokenStore.refresh();
  if (refreshed) socket.connect();
  else signOut();
});
```

The server checks the token before accepting the connection. A refused connection fires `connect_error` with one of these messages:

| `err.message` | Cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `Authentication required` | No `auth.token` and no `Authorization` header | Send the access token. |
| `Authentication failed` | The token is malformed, expired, badly signed or a refresh token, or the check hit a server error | Get a new access token with [`refreshToken`](#refreshtoken) (admins: [`adminRefreshToken`](#adminrefreshtoken)), then call `socket.connect()`. Give up after a few tries and sign the user out. |
| `Invalid token` | The token is genuine but fails the same account checks as a GraphQL request: for example the account was deleted, deactivated, suspended or banned, the token was signed out with [`logout`](#logout) or [`adminLogout`](#adminlogout), the password was changed or reset after the token was issued, an admin ended the account's sessions, or the account's role changed (for example after [`becomeProvider`](#becomeprovider) or [`updateAdminRole`](#updateadminrole)) | Refresh the token or sign in again. Sign-in shows suspended and banned users the reason. |

When the server refuses a connection, `socket.io-client` doesn't retry on its own: call `socket.connect()` once the token is fixed. Ordinary drops (network changes, a server restart, the app going to the background) reconnect automatically with backoff.

After accepting a connection, the server:

1. Adds the socket to the room `user:<userId>` and attaches the event handlers. Both happen straight away, so events you emit as soon as `connect` fires are handled.
2. Records the socket in Redis and marks the user online for 3 minutes.
3. Sends `user:online` to the people who share a conversation with the user.

Steps 2 and 3 finish shortly after `connect`. When Redis is unavailable the socket still works, but the user doesn't show as online.

Other things to plan for:

- **Sessions are checked again while connected.** About every 5 minutes, the server repeats the account checks for each connected socket and checks whether its access token has expired. When either fails, the socket receives `session:ended` and is disconnected. Anything that makes a new connection fail with `Invalid token`, such as a suspension, a ban, a password change or signing the token out, ends open sockets within about 5 minutes. Still call `socket.disconnect()` on sign-out. After [`becomeProvider`](#becomeprovider), reconnect with the new access token.
- **Rooms belong to one connection.** After a reconnect the server adds the socket to `user:<userId>` again, but you must emit `conversation:join` again for an open chat.
- **Missed events aren't replayed.** After every reconnect, refetch what the open screen shows, for example [`conversationMessages`](#conversationmessages) or [`booking`](#booking).
- **Several devices** each have their own socket, and each receives the events for `user:<userId>`.
- **Browser clients (the admin dashboard):** the allowed origins come from `WEBSOCKET_CORS_ORIGINS` or, when that's empty, from `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, the list the GraphQL endpoint uses. If the dashboard's origin isn't allowed, the polling transport fails: connect with `transports: ['websocket']`, or ask for the origin to be added. Native apps send no `Origin` header and aren't affected.
- **Realtime needs the custom server.** Socket.IO only runs under `npm run start:ws` (production, as deployed on Render) or `npm run dev:ws` (local). Under `npm run dev` or `npm start`, GraphQL works but socket connections fail.
- **Realtime needs Redis.** GraphQL operations publish their socket events through Redis. Without Redis those events never arrive and presence isn't recorded, although connected sockets keep handling their own events. The API itself keeps working, so the app must cope without the socket (see [Fallbacks when the socket is disconnected](#fallbacks-when-the-socket-is-disconnected)).

### Rooms

| Room | How a socket joins | Events it receives |
|---|---|---|
| `user:<userId>` | Automatically, on connect | `notification:new`; `booking:created`, `booking:accepted`, `booking:rejected`, `booking:started`, `booking:completed`, `booking:confirmed`, `booking:cancelled`; `user:online` and `user:offline` for people who share a conversation with the user |
| `conversation:<conversationId>` | Emit `conversation:join`. Leave with `conversation:leave`, or by disconnecting. | `message:new`, `message:deleted`, `typing:update`, `messages:read`, `user:joined`, `user:left` |
| None: only the socket concerned | Always | `message:sent`, `presence:status`, `session:ended`, `error` |

Join a conversation's room when its chat screen opens and leave when the screen closes. Only sockets in the room receive `message:new`. For the chat list and the unread badge, use `notification:new` (type `NEW_MESSAGE`), push notifications and queries.

### Client to server events

| Event | Payload | What comes back |
|---|---|---|
| `conversation:join` | `{ conversationId }` | `user:joined` to others in the room; `error` on failure |
| `conversation:leave` | `{ conversationId }` | `user:left` to others in the room |
| `message:send` | `{ conversationId, content, attachments?, tempId? }` | `message:new` to the room and `message:sent` to you; `error` on failure |
| `messages:read` | `{ conversationId, messageIds }` | `messages:read` to others in the room; `error` on failure |
| `typing:start` | `{ conversationId }` | `typing:update` with `isTyping: true` to others in the room |
| `typing:stop` | `{ conversationId }` | `typing:update` with `isTyping: false` to others in the room |
| `presence:check` | `{ userIds }` | `presence:status` to you |
| `heartbeat` | none | nothing |

None of these events uses Socket.IO acknowledgement callbacks. Replies arrive as separate events. A payload without the fields shown is ignored, or answered with `error` where the event lists errors.

#### `conversation:join`

```json
{ "conversationId": "66e2a1f4c3b2a10012ab34cd" }
```

- **Checks:** you're a participant of the conversation. Archived conversations can be joined. Blocks aren't checked.
- **On success:** the socket joins `conversation:<conversationId>`, and other sockets already in the room get `user:joined`. You get no confirmation.
- **Errors**, sent as an `error` event with `event: "conversation:join"`:

| `message` | Cause |
|---|---|
| `Conversation not found or access denied` | Unknown conversation, a malformed ID, or you aren't a participant |
| `Failed to join conversation` | Server error |

#### `conversation:leave`

```json
{ "conversationId": "66e2a1f4c3b2a10012ab34cd" }
```

- **Checks:** the socket must be in the room; otherwise nothing happens.
- **Effect:** the socket leaves the room, and the other sockets in it get `user:left`. No errors.

#### `message:send`

```json
{
  "conversationId": "66e2a1f4c3b2a10012ab34cd",
  "content": "I can be there by 2pm tomorrow.",
  "attachments": ["https://res.cloudinary.com/easykonnet-demo/image/upload/v1789218000/sample.jpg"],
  "tempId": "local-7f3a"
}
```

- **Fields:** `content` is required; send `""` for an attachment-only message. `attachments` is optional: up to 10 URLs of files uploaded to Easykonnet's Cloudinary account. `tempId` is optional: your own ID for this message, a string or a number, returned in `message:sent` and in any `error` about this message. Replies (`replyToId`) can't be sent this way; use [`sendMessage`](#sendmessage).
- **Limit:** 60 messages a minute per user, shared with the [`sendMessage`](#sendmessage) and [`startConversation`](#startconversation) mutations, so all three count toward the same 60. Every attempt counts, including refused ones. Over the limit the message isn't sent, and `error` arrives with `code: "RATE_LIMITED"` and `retryAfter` in seconds.
- **Checks:** the message goes through the same code as the [`sendMessage`](#sendmessage) mutation:
  1. You must be a participant.
  2. Neither of you may have blocked the other.
  3. `content` and `attachments` can't both be empty. The cleaned text (step 5) can have up to 5,000 characters, and each attachment must be a file uploaded to Easykonnet.
  4. When the server requires community terms acceptance (`REQUIRE_TERMS_ACCEPTANCE`), you must have accepted the current version.
  5. The text is trimmed and saved as plain text: HTML tags are removed, along with the contents of `script` and `style` elements, `&` and quotes are kept as typed, and a stray `<` or `>` is saved as `&lt;` or `&gt;`. Blocked words are replaced with asterisks. Messages with blocked words or bank details are flagged for admins (see [Chat, safety and moderation](#chat-safety-and-moderation)).
  6. Every other participant gets an in-app `NEW_MESSAGE` notification (also sent as `notification:new`) and a push notification.
- **Emits:** `message:new` to everyone in the conversation's room, including your own sockets if they joined. Then `message:sent` to this socket. Your typing indicator is cleared on the server, but no `typing:update` is sent for it.
- **Errors**, sent as an `error` event with `event: "message:send"`, plus the message's `tempId` when it has one:

| `message` | Cause |
|---|---|
| `Too many messages. Please try again in <n> seconds.` | Over the limit. The event also has `code: "RATE_LIMITED"` and `retryAfter`. |
| `Conversation not found or access denied` | Unknown conversation, a malformed ID, or you aren't a participant |
| `You can't send messages in this conversation` | One of you has blocked the other |
| `Message content or attachments required` | Empty `content` and no attachments |
| `Messages can be at most 5000 characters` | The cleaned text is longer than 5,000 characters |
| `A message can have at most 10 attachments` | More than 10 attachments |
| `Attachments must be files uploaded to Easykonnet` | An attachment isn't a file on Easykonnet's Cloudinary account |
| `Please accept the community terms before posting` | Terms acceptance is required and the user hasn't accepted the current version |
| `Failed to send message` | Anything else, for example a missing `content` field, `attachments` that isn't a list of strings, or a server error |

Any other refusal from [`sendMessage`](#sendmessage) arrives with the same message text.

Match `message:sent` and `error` to the message by `tempId`. Without a `tempId`, send one message at a time and wait for `message:sent`, or an `error` with `event: "message:send"`, before sending the next.

#### `messages:read`

```json
{
  "conversationId": "66e2a1f4c3b2a10012ab34cd",
  "messageIds": ["66e2b0c1c3b2a10012ab3501", "66e2b0d9c3b2a10012ab3502"]
}
```

- **Checks:** you must be a participant of the conversation. Entries in `messageIds` that aren't message IDs are skipped; when none are left, nothing happens.
- **Effect:** the same as [`markMessagesAsRead`](#markmessagesasread) with these IDs. The listed messages that belong to this conversation and were sent by someone else are marked read: you're added to their `readBy` (once), `status` becomes `READ` and `readAt` is set. Messages you had already read are left as they were. Unread counts ([`unreadMessageCount`](#unreadmessagecount) and `myConversations.unreadCount`) go down accordingly.
- **Emits:** `messages:read` to the other sockets in the room, with the message IDs you sent, without duplicates or skipped entries.
- **Errors**, sent as an `error` event with `event: "messages:read"`:

| `message` | Cause |
|---|---|
| `Conversation not found or access denied` | Unknown conversation, a malformed ID, or you aren't a participant |
| `Failed to mark messages as read` | Server error |

#### `typing:start` and `typing:stop`

```json
{ "conversationId": "66e2a1f4c3b2a10012ab34cd" }
```

- **Checks:** you must be a participant of the conversation; otherwise the event is ignored, without an error. Join the room first, so you also receive the other person's updates. An `isTyping` field in the payload is ignored.
- **Emits:** `typing:update` to the other sockets in the room, with `isTyping` true for `typing:start` and false for `typing:stop`.
- **Sending:** send `typing:start` at most every 3 seconds while the user types, and `typing:stop` when they stop or send.
- **Receiving:** the server never announces on its own that typing has stopped. Hide the indicator after 5 seconds without a new `typing:update`, or when a `message:new` arrives from that user. No errors.

#### `presence:check`

```json
{ "userIds": ["66e29f00c3b2a10012ab3400", "66e29f55c3b2a10012ab3455"] }
```

- **Checks:** none; any user IDs can be asked about. `userIds` must be an array, or nothing comes back. Entries that aren't strings are left out.
- **Emits:** `presence:status` to this socket.
- **Who counts as online:** a user whose socket connected, or who sent `heartbeat`, in the last 3 minutes. The status is cleared when their last socket disconnects.

#### `heartbeat`

No payload and no reply. It keeps the user shown as online for another 3 minutes. Send it every 60 seconds while the socket is connected and the app is in the foreground, and stop when the app goes to the background. Without it, a connected user shows as offline to `presence:check` 3 minutes after connecting.

### Server to client events

| Event | Sent when | Received by |
|---|---|---|
| `message:new` | A message is saved: [`sendMessage`](#sendmessage), `message:send`, or the first message of [`startConversation`](#startconversation) or [`startSupportChat`](#startsupportchat) | Every socket in `conversation:<id>` |
| `message:sent` | Your `message:send` succeeded | The sending socket |
| `message:deleted` | A sender deleted a message with [`deleteMessage`](#deletemessage) | Every socket in `conversation:<id>` |
| `messages:read` | A participant emitted `messages:read` | The other sockets in `conversation:<id>` |
| `typing:update` | A participant emitted `typing:start` or `typing:stop` | The other sockets in `conversation:<id>` |
| `user:joined` | Someone joined the conversation's room | The other sockets in `conversation:<id>` |
| `user:left` | A socket in the room emitted `conversation:leave` | The other sockets in `conversation:<id>` |
| `user:online` | One of a user's sockets connects | `user:<id>` of everyone who shares a conversation with that user |
| `user:offline` | A user's last socket disconnects | `user:<id>` of everyone who shares a conversation with that user |
| `presence:status` | Reply to `presence:check` | The socket that asked |
| `notification:new` | An in-app notification is created for the user, including admin broadcasts | `user:<id>` of the recipient |
| `booking:created` | [`createBooking`](#createbooking) | The provider |
| `booking:accepted` | [`acceptBooking`](#acceptbooking) | The customer |
| `booking:rejected` | [`rejectBooking`](#rejectbooking) | The customer |
| `booking:started` | [`startService`](#startservice) | The customer |
| `booking:completed` | [`completeService`](#completeservice) | The customer |
| `booking:confirmed` | [`confirmServiceDelivery`](#confirmservicedelivery) | The provider |
| `booking:cancelled` | [`cancelBooking`](#cancelbooking) or [`adminCancelBooking`](#admincancelbooking) | The provider when the customer cancels; both parties when an admin cancels |
| `session:ended` | The periodic session check failed; the socket is disconnected straight after | That socket |
| `error` | `conversation:join`, `message:send` or `messages:read` failed | The socket that sent it |

Dates in socket payloads are ISO 8601 strings, like the dates in GraphQL results.

#### `message:new`

```json
{
  "id": "66e2b0c1c3b2a10012ab3501",
  "conversationId": "66e2a1f4c3b2a10012ab34cd",
  "senderId": "66e29f00c3b2a10012ab3400",
  "senderRole": "SERVICE_USER",
  "senderName": "Ada Obi",
  "content": "I can be there by 2pm tomorrow.",
  "attachments": [],
  "status": "SENT",
  "createdAt": "2026-09-12T10:15:30.000Z"
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | Message ID. The sender's own sockets receive the message too, so use the ID to avoid showing it twice. |
| `conversationId` | The conversation |
| `senderId` | The sender's user ID |
| `senderRole` | `SERVICE_USER`, `SERVICE_PROVIDER`, `ADMIN` or `SUPER_ADMIN` |
| `senderName` | The sender's first and last name, or `Someone` if both are empty |
| `content` | The saved text, as plain text: HTML tags removed, `&` and quotes as typed, a stray `<` or `>` as `&lt;` or `&gt;`, and blocked words replaced with asterisks. Show it as text, turning `&lt;` and `&gt;` back into `<` and `>`. |
| `attachments` | File URLs, as sent |
| `status` | Always `SENT` |
| `createdAt` | ISO 8601 |

`replyToId`, `readBy` and `sender` aren't included; load them with [`conversationMessages`](#conversationmessages) when needed.

#### `message:sent`

```json
{ "messageId": "66e2b0c1c3b2a10012ab3501", "tempId": "local-7f3a" }
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `messageId` | ID of the saved message |
| `tempId` | The `tempId` sent with this `message:send`. When the message had none: the `tempId` query parameter the socket connected with (`io(url, { query: { tempId } })`), which is the same for every message on that connection. Absent when neither was given. |

It arrives after the `message:new` for the same message.

#### `message:deleted`

```json
{ "conversationId": "66e2a1f4c3b2a10012ab34cd", "messageId": "66e2b0c1c3b2a10012ab3501" }
```

- **When:** the sender deleted the message with [`deleteMessage`](#deletemessage). It goes to every socket in the room, the sender's included.
- **What to do:** remove the message from the open chat. [`conversationMessages`](#conversationmessages) no longer returns it, and an unread `NEW_MESSAGE` notification for it now reads "This message was deleted".

#### `messages:read` (to other participants)

```json
{
  "conversationId": "66e2a1f4c3b2a10012ab34cd",
  "messageIds": ["66e2b0c1c3b2a10012ab3501"],
  "readBy": "66e29f55c3b2a10012ab3455",
  "readAt": "2026-09-12T10:16:02.120Z"
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `conversationId` | The conversation |
| `messageIds` | The message IDs the reader sent, without duplicates or malformed entries. IDs of the reader's own messages, or of messages in another conversation, are listed but weren't marked read. |
| `readBy` | The reader's user ID |
| `readAt` | When the server handled the event |

Only the socket event produces it. [`markMessagesAsRead`](#markmessagesasread) and [`conversationMessages`](#conversationmessages) mark messages read without telling anyone.

#### `typing:update`

```json
{
  "userId": "66e29f55c3b2a10012ab3455",
  "userName": "Tunde Bello",
  "conversationId": "66e2a1f4c3b2a10012ab34cd",
  "isTyping": true
}
```

- `userName` is the user's first and last name, or `Someone` if both are empty, as they were when the user's socket connected.

#### `user:joined` and `user:left`

```json
{
  "userId": "66e29f55c3b2a10012ab3455",
  "userName": "Tunde Bello",
  "conversationId": "66e2a1f4c3b2a10012ab34cd"
}
```

- **`userName`** is the same as in `typing:update`.
- **`user:joined`** follows a successful `conversation:join`, including a rejoin after a reconnect.
- **`user:left`** follows `conversation:leave` from a socket that was in the room, never a disconnect. Don't use either event for presence.

#### `user:online`

```json
{ "userId": "66e29f55c3b2a10012ab3455", "userName": "Tunde Bello" }
```

- **Recipients:** everyone who shares a conversation with the user, archived conversations included, on each of their sockets. For a user with more than 1,000 conversations, the people in the 1,000 most recently active ones.
- **When:** each time one of the user's sockets connects. Reconnects and second devices count.
- **Already online:** you get no `user:online` for people who were online before you connected. Ask with `presence:check`.
- `userName` is the same as in `typing:update`.

#### `user:offline`

```json
{
  "userId": "66e29f55c3b2a10012ab3455",
  "userName": "Tunde Bello",
  "lastSeen": "2026-09-12T11:02:44.518Z"
}
```

- **Recipients:** the same people as `user:online`.
- **When:** a socket disconnects and the user has no other socket connected. Sockets cut off by a server restart stop counting within 3 minutes.
- **Server restarts:** a socket cut off by a restart sends no `user:offline`. If the user doesn't reconnect, they show as offline to `presence:check` within 3 minutes, so confirm with `presence:check` when a contact seems online for too long.

#### `presence:status`

```json
{ "66e29f00c3b2a10012ab3400": true, "66e29f55c3b2a10012ab3455": false }
```

- One key per user ID you asked about, `true` when online.

#### `notification:new`

```json
{
  "id": "66e2d1a0c3b2a10012ab3700",
  "type": "NEW_MESSAGE",
  "title": "New Message",
  "message": "I can be there by 2pm tomorrow.",
  "entityType": "conversation",
  "entityId": "66e2a1f4c3b2a10012ab34cd",
  "metadata": null,
  "createdAt": "2026-09-12T10:15:30.000Z"
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | The in-app notification's ID, as returned by [`myNotifications`](#mynotifications) |
| `type` | The notification type, for example `NEW_MESSAGE`, `BOOKING_ACCEPTED` or `SYSTEM_ANNOUNCEMENT` |
| `title`, `message` | As saved |
| `entityType`, `entityId` | What the notification is about, for example `conversation` and the conversation's ID. Admin broadcasts have `entityType` `broadcast` and `entityId` `null`. Either can be `null`. |
| `metadata` | An object, such as the object from a broadcast's `metadataJson`, or `null` |
| `createdAt` | ISO 8601 |

- **Sent for every in-app notification** created for the user, including admin broadcasts, to the sockets connected at that moment.
- When it arrives, update the notification list and badge, or refetch [`unreadNotificationCount`](#unreadnotificationcount) and [`myNotifications`](#mynotifications).

#### Booking events

`booking:created`, `booking:accepted`, `booking:rejected`, `booking:started`, `booking:completed`, `booking:confirmed` and `booking:cancelled` share one payload:

```json
{
  "bookingId": "66e2c3d4c3b2a10012ab3600",
  "booking": {
    "id": "66e2c3d4c3b2a10012ab3600",
    "status": "ACCEPTED",
    "scheduledDate": "2026-09-20T00:00:00.000Z",
    "scheduledTime": "14:00",
    "totalAmount": 15000,
    "cancellationReason": null,
    "updatedAt": "2026-09-12T10:20:00.000Z",
    "service": { "id": "66e2a9b0c3b2a10012ab3520", "name": "Deep home cleaning" },
    "provider": { "id": "66e2a800c3b2a10012ab3510", "businessName": "Sparkle Cleaners" },
    "user": { "id": "66e29f00c3b2a10012ab3400", "firstName": "Ada", "lastName": "Obi", "profilePhoto": null }
  }
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `bookingId` | Same as `booking.id` |
| `booking.status` | The status after the change: `PENDING` for `booking:created`, `ACCEPTED`, `REJECTED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `COMPLETED` (also for `booking:confirmed`) or `CANCELLED` |
| `booking.scheduledDate` | The booking day, as midnight UTC |
| `booking.scheduledTime` | `HH:mm`, as the customer entered it |
| `booking.totalAmount` | What the customer pays, in naira |
| `booking.cancellationReason` | For `booking:rejected`, the provider's reason. For `booking:cancelled`, the customer's reason, or `[Admin] <reason>` when an admin cancelled. Otherwise `null`. |
| `booking.updatedAt` | When the booking last changed |
| `booking.service` | `id` and `name` |
| `booking.provider` | The provider profile's `id` (not a user ID) and `businessName` |
| `booking.user` | The customer: `id`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `profilePhoto` |

| Event | Operation | Recipient | Also sent |
|---|---|---|---|
| `booking:created` | [`createBooking`](#createbooking) | Provider | In-app `BOOKING_CREATED` ("New Booking Request"), push |
| `booking:accepted` | [`acceptBooking`](#acceptbooking) | Customer | In-app `BOOKING_ACCEPTED`, push |
| `booking:rejected` | [`rejectBooking`](#rejectbooking) | Customer | In-app `BOOKING_REJECTED`, push |
| `booking:started` | [`startService`](#startservice) | Customer | In-app `BOOKING_STARTED`; no push |
| `booking:completed` | [`completeService`](#completeservice) | Customer | In-app `BOOKING_COMPLETED`, push |
| `booking:confirmed` | [`confirmServiceDelivery`](#confirmservicedelivery) | Provider | In-app `BOOKING_COMPLETED` ("Delivery Confirmed", with when the payment will be released), push |
| `booking:cancelled` | [`cancelBooking`](#cancelbooking) | Provider | In-app `BOOKING_CANCELLED`, push |
| `booking:cancelled` | [`adminCancelBooking`](#admincancelbooking) | Customer and provider | In-app `BOOKING_CANCELLED`, push |

- **In-app notifications** in this table also arrive as `notification:new`.
- **Not covered:** payments, refunds, releases and disputes have no booking event.
- **Payment details** aren't in the payload; fetch [`booking`](#booking) for them.

#### `session:ended`

```json
{
  "reason": "SESSION_REVOKED",
  "message": "Your session is no longer valid. Refresh your access token or sign in again."
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `reason` | `TOKEN_EXPIRED`: the access token the socket connected with has expired. `SESSION_REVOKED`: the token fails the account checks, for the same reasons a new connection gets `Invalid token`. |
| `message` | `Your access token has expired. Refresh it and connect again.` or `Your session is no longer valid. Refresh your access token or sign in again.` |

- **When:** the server checks each connected socket about every 5 minutes (between 4.5 and 5.5 minutes apart). A check that can't run, for example while the database is unreachable, leaves the socket connected until the next one.
- **Then:** the server disconnects the socket, and `socket.io-client` doesn't reconnect by itself. Refresh the token ([`refreshToken`](#refreshtoken), admins [`adminRefreshToken`](#adminrefreshtoken)) and call `socket.connect()`. If the refresh fails, sign the user out; sign-in shows suspended and banned users the reason.

#### `error`

```json
{ "message": "Conversation not found or access denied", "event": "conversation:join" }
```

```json
{
  "message": "Too many messages. Please try again in 42 seconds.",
  "event": "message:send",
  "code": "RATE_LIMITED",
  "retryAfter": 42,
  "tempId": "local-7f3a"
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `message` | What went wrong; the messages are listed under `conversation:join`, `message:send` and `messages:read` |
| `event` | The event that failed: `conversation:join`, `message:send` or `messages:read` |
| `tempId` | `message:send` only: the message's `tempId`, when it has one (see `message:sent`) |
| `code` | `RATE_LIMITED` when `message:send` is over its limit; absent otherwise |
| `retryAfter` | With `RATE_LIMITED`: seconds until a message can be sent again |

### Fallbacks when the socket is disconnected

While the app is in the background, rely on push notifications. In the foreground, poll only the screen that's open. When the socket reconnects, stop polling and refetch once. Polling counts toward the per-user query limit, which is 300 queries a minute by default (see Part 1).

| Screen | What the socket would have sent | Poll | How often |
|---|---|---|---|
| Open chat | `message:new`, `message:deleted`, `messages:read` | [`conversationMessages`](#conversationmessages), page 1. Loading a page marks it read, so poll only while the chat is on screen. | Every 5 to 10 seconds |
| Chat list and unread badge | `notification:new` (`NEW_MESSAGE`) | [`myConversations`](#myconversations), [`unreadMessageCount`](#unreadmessagecount) | On focus, then every 30 to 60 seconds |
| Booking details | `booking:*` | [`booking`](#booking) | Every 15 to 30 seconds |
| Customer's bookings | `booking:*` | [`myBookings`](#mybookings) | On focus |
| Provider's new requests | `booking:created` | [`providerBookings`](#providerbookings) with `status: PENDING`, [`providerBookingStats`](#providerbookingstats) | On focus, then every 30 to 60 seconds while open |
| Notifications | `notification:new` | [`unreadNotificationCount`](#unreadnotificationcount), [`myNotifications`](#mynotifications) | On focus, then every 60 seconds |
| After checkout | No payment event | [`verifyPayment`](#verifypayment) once, then [`paymentByBooking`](#paymentbybooking) | Every 5 seconds for up to a minute |
| Wallet and withdrawals | `notification:new`, for the changes that create a notification | [`myWallet`](#mywallet), [`myWithdrawals`](#mywithdrawals) | On focus |
| Provider verification and services | `notification:new`, for the changes that create a notification | [`myVerificationStatus`](#myverificationstatus), [`myServices`](#myservices) | On focus |
| Presence and typing | `user:online`, `user:offline`, `typing:update` | Nothing to poll: hide the indicators | |

## Guides

Each guide is a journey in order: the operations to call, what to show, and the rules that connect them. Every argument and error of each operation is in Part 3. All amounts are in naira.

### Your first session as a customer

1. **Sign up** with [`register`](#register).
   - Password: 8 to 128 characters, with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number and a special character.
   - First and last name: 2 to 100 characters (letters, numbers, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes and full stops), with no blocked words, phone numbers, email addresses or account numbers (`INAPPROPRIATE_CONTENT`, `CONTACT_DETAILS_NOT_ALLOWED`).
   - Phone is optional. Local (`0801 234 5678`) and international (`+2348012345678`) forms are both accepted, and it's stored as `+2348012345678`. Other numbers fail with `Invalid phone number`.
   - The account is created with status `PENDING`, and a 6-digit code is emailed. Show "Enter the code we sent to ada.obi@example.com".
   - Registering again with an email that isn't verified yet sends a new code; the first attempt's name, phone and password are kept. A verified email gets `USER_ALREADY_EXISTS`.
   - Limits: 5 registrations per email per hour, and 5 attempts per minute.

2. **Verify the email** with [`verifyEmail`](#verifyemail).
   - The code lasts 10 minutes (`OTP_EXPIRED`). [`resendVerificationOtp`](#resendverificationotp) sends a new one, up to 3 times in 5 minutes.
   - A wrong code returns `INVALID_OTP`. After 5 wrong codes, attempts are refused for 10 minutes (`RATE_LIMITED`).
   - On success the account becomes `ACTIVE`, and the response includes tokens that work like the ones [`login`](#login) returns: store them. Its `user` has every field.
   - For an account that was suspended or banned before it was verified, the tokens are `null`; sign-in shows the reason.

3. **Sign in** with [`login`](#login).
   - Store both tokens securely and send `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` with every request. Access tokens last 7 days and refresh tokens 30 days, by default.
   - When a request returns `UNAUTHENTICATED`, get a new access token with [`refreshToken`](#refreshtoken). It returns a new access token only (up to 120 calls a minute). When it fails, send the user to sign in.
   - [`login`](#login) returns every `User` field, including `pushEnabled`. Load `providerProfile` from [`me`](#me).

   ```graphql
   mutation SignIn($input: LoginInput!) {
     login(input: $input) {
       accessToken
       refreshToken
       user { id email firstName lastName role activeRole status }
     }
   }
   ```
   Variables:
   ```json
   { "input": { "email": "ada.obi@example.com", "password": "Sunny-Day-2026" } }
   ```

   | Error | Show |
   |---|---|
   | `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` | "Wrong email or password". `extensions.attemptsRemaining` counts down after a wrong password. |
   | `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED` | The code screen from step 2 (`extensions.requiresVerification` is true) |
   | `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` | "Try again in N minutes": 5 wrong passwords lock the account for 30 minutes. |
   | `RATE_LIMITED` | "Too many attempts": 10 attempts per account every 15 minutes, and 100 from one IP address. |
   | `USER_SUSPENDED`, `ACCOUNT_BANNED` | The message, with a way to contact support |

   Signing in with the right password reactivates a deactivated account. Deactivating with [`deactivateMyAccount`](#deactivatemyaccount) ends every session.

4. **Set up the session.**
   - Register the device for push with [`registerPushToken`](#registerpushtoken), using the OneSignal subscription ID. An account keeps up to 10 devices, and pushes go to all of them. On sign-out, call [`unregisterPushToken`](#unregisterpushtoken) with this device's ID; without an ID it removes every device. If the user switched push off, registering a device keeps it off.
   - Load the profile with [`me`](#me).
   - Check [`termsStatus`](#termsstatus). If `mustAccept` is true, show the community terms and call [`acceptTerms`](#acceptterms) with `currentVersion` (see [Chat, safety and moderation](#chat-safety-and-moderation)).
   - Connect the socket (see [Connecting](#connecting)).

5. **Browse and search.**
   - [`categories`](#categories) for category filters.
   - [`nearbyServices`](#nearbyservices): active services from verified providers within `radiusKm` of the user (default 25, maximum 100), nearest first, each with `distanceKm`. Providers without saved coordinates never appear in nearby results.
   - [`nearbyProviders`](#nearbyproviders): verified providers nearby. It sorts by rating unless you pass `sortBy`: `NEAREST` sorts by distance, nearest first, and `NEWEST` puts the newest providers first.
   - [`services`](#services): text search (`filters.search` matches name or description, ignoring case), with category, city, state, price and optional distance filters. Only active services.
   - [`providers`](#providers): browse verified providers, with filters and sorting.
   - Details: [`service`](#service), [`providerProfile`](#providerprofile) (with `activeServices`), [`providerReviews`](#providerreviews) and [`providerRating`](#providerrating). Save favourites with [`toggleFavourite`](#togglefavourite).
   - While signed in, lists leave out your own listings and providers you've blocked.

   ```graphql
   query NearbyCleaning($input: NearbyServicesInput!) {
     nearbyServices(input: $input) {
       items {
         id
         name
         price
         duration
         distanceKm
         category { name }
         provider { id businessName verificationStatus }
       }
       total
       hasNextPage
       radiusKm
     }
   }
   ```
   Variables:
   ```json
   {
     "input": {
       "latitude": 6.4541,
       "longitude": 3.4247,
       "radiusKm": 10,
       "search": "cleaning",
       "pagination": { "page": 1, "limit": 20 }
     }
   }
   ```

6. **Book** with [`createBooking`](#createbooking).
   - Send `scheduledDate` as `YYYY-MM-DD` and `scheduledTime` as 24-hour `HH:mm`; other formats are refused (`INVALID_BOOKING_TIME`). The pair is read as Lagos time: `14:00` means 14:00 in Lagos.
   - The time must be at least 2 hours ahead and no more than 30 days ahead (`INVALID_BOOKING_TIME`).
   - The service must be `ACTIVE` (`SERVICE_NOT_AVAILABLE`) and its provider verified (`PROVIDER_NOT_VERIFIED`). You can't book your own service (`SELF_BOOKING_NOT_ALLOWED`) or a provider when either of you has blocked the other (`BOOKING_NOT_ALLOWED`).
   - `totalAmount` is the service price, and it's what the customer pays. Easykonnet's commission comes out of the provider's share; it isn't added on top.
   - The booking starts as `PENDING`, and the provider gets `booking:created`, an in-app `BOOKING_CREATED` notification and a push.
   - Show "Request sent: waiting for Sparkle Cleaners to accept". Offer [`updateBooking`](#updatebooking) (date, time, address and notes, while `PENDING`) and [`cancelBooking`](#cancelbooking).

   ```graphql
   mutation BookService($input: CreateBookingInput!) {
     createBooking(input: $input) {
       id
       status
       scheduledDate
       scheduledTime
       totalAmount
       service { name }
       provider { businessName }
     }
   }
   ```
   Variables:
   ```json
   {
     "input": {
       "serviceId": "66e2a9b0c3b2a10012ab3520",
       "scheduledDate": "2026-09-20",
       "scheduledTime": "14:00",
       "address": "12 Admiralty Way",
       "city": "Lekki",
       "state": "Lagos",
       "notes": "Two-bedroom flat, third floor."
     }
   }
   ```

7. **Wait for the provider.**
   - **Accepted:** the customer gets `booking:accepted` on the socket, a push ("Booking Accepted!") and an in-app `BOOKING_ACCEPTED` notification.
   - **Declined:** `booking:rejected` arrives; show `cancellationReason`.
   - **Without the socket:** refresh [`booking`](#booking).
   - **No expiry:** pending bookings stay pending until the provider answers or the customer cancels.

8. **Pay** once the booking is `ACCEPTED`. See [Taking payment](#taking-payment).
   - Card, bank or USSD: [`initializePayment`](#initializepayment), open the checkout, then [`verifyPayment`](#verifypayment) when the app reopens.
   - Wallet balance: [`payWithWallet`](#paywithwallet).
   - The money is held until the job is done. The provider can't start the job before payment, and an accepted, unpaid booking doesn't expire.

9. **Talk to the provider.** Open the booking's chat with [`bookingConversation`](#bookingconversation), which creates it if needed. Emit `conversation:join`, then send with `message:send` or [`sendMessage`](#sendmessage).

10. **Follow the job.**
    - **Started:** `booking:started` and an in-app notification, but no push. Show "In progress".
    - **Completed:** `booking:completed`, a push and an in-app notification. Show "Job done: confirm it, or report a problem".

11. **Confirm the job is done** with [`confirmServiceDelivery`](#confirmservicedelivery).
    - **Requirements:** the booking is `COMPLETED` and paid (`PAYMENT_NOT_COMPLETED`). It can be confirmed only once (`ALREADY_CONFIRMED`).
    - **Effect:** the response has `customerConfirmedAt`, and `paymentReleaseAt` set 24 hours later. Show "Sparkle Cleaners will be paid on <paymentReleaseAt>. Report a problem before then."
    - **No confirmation:** the provider is paid 7 days after `completedAt`.
    - **A problem instead:** open a dispute with [`createDispute`](#createdispute) before the payment is released (see [Disputes](#disputes)).

    ```graphql
    mutation ConfirmJob($bookingId: ID!) {
      confirmServiceDelivery(bookingId: $bookingId) {
        id
        status
        customerConfirmedAt
        paymentReleaseAt
      }
    }
    ```
    Variables:
    ```json
    { "bookingId": "66e2c3d4c3b2a10012ab3600" }
    ```

12. **Review.** Check [`canReviewBooking`](#canreviewbooking), then call [`createReview`](#createreview).
    - **When:** the booking must be `COMPLETED`. Reviews open as soon as the provider completes the job; the customer doesn't have to confirm first.
    - **Content:** one review per booking (`ALREADY_REVIEWED`), a whole-number rating from 1 to 5, and a comment of up to 1,000 characters without blocked words or contact details. When terms acceptance is required, the current terms must be accepted.
    - **Changes:** the customer can edit the review for 24 hours with [`updateReview`](#updatereview). The provider can reply once with [`respondToReview`](#respondtoreview). The provider gets an in-app `REVIEW_RECEIVED` notification and a push for each new review, and the customer gets `REVIEW_RESPONSE` and a push when the provider replies, unless the review is hidden.

### Becoming and working as a provider

1. **Become a provider** with [`becomeProvider`](#becomeprovider).
   - **Requirements:** the account is `ACTIVE`, the email is verified, and the role is `SERVICE_USER` (`ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE`, `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED`, `ALREADY_PROVIDER`, `INVALID_ROLE`).
   - **Input rules:** `businessName` 2 to 100 characters; `businessDescription` optional, 10 to 250 characters; `address` required, up to 255; `city`, `state` and `country` 2 to 100. Business name and description can't contain blocked words or contact details.
   - **Location:** send `latitude` and `longitude`, or the provider never appears in nearby searches.
   - **Result:** the role becomes `SERVICE_PROVIDER` and a provider profile is created as `UNVERIFIED`.
   - **Replace both stored tokens with the ones returned, straight away.** The old access token carries the old role, so every request with it now fails with `UNAUTHENTICATED`, and a socket reconnecting with it gets `Invalid token`. Reconnect the socket with the new access token.

   ```graphql
   mutation BecomeProvider($input: BecomeProviderInput!) {
     becomeProvider(input: $input) {
       accessToken
       refreshToken
       user {
         id
         role
         providerProfile { id businessName verificationStatus }
       }
     }
   }
   ```
   Variables:
   ```json
   {
     "input": {
       "businessName": "Sparkle Cleaners",
       "businessDescription": "Home and office cleaning across Lekki and Victoria Island.",
       "address": "5 Fola Osibo Road",
       "city": "Lekki",
       "state": "Lagos",
       "country": "Nigeria",
       "latitude": 6.4355,
       "longitude": 3.4521
     }
   }
   ```

2. **Complete the profile.**
   - [`updateProviderProfile`](#updateproviderprofile) changes any profile field. Its `profilePhoto` sets the account photo to a URL, and an empty value removes it; [`uploadProfilePhoto`](#uploadprofilephoto) uploads one.
   - Once the provider is verified, the profile stays live when edited. Changing the business name or description creates an automatic report for admins to check.

3. **Add gallery images and documents.** Uploads are limited to 20 a minute, and base64 uploads must fit the request size limit (see uploads in Part 1).
   - **Gallery:** [`uploadProviderImages`](#uploadproviderimages), sent as base64 in the GraphQL request, up to 10 images in total (jpg, jpeg, png, webp or gif). Remove one with [`removeProviderImage`](#removeproviderimage).
   - **Documents:** [`uploadProviderDocuments`](#uploadproviderdocuments) as base64, or upload each file with [`getDocumentUploadParams`](#getdocumentuploadparams) and save them with [`addProviderDocuments`](#addproviderdocuments). Up to 5 in total (jpg, jpeg, png, pdf, doc or docx), for example an ID and a CAC certificate. Remove one with [`removeProviderDocument`](#removeproviderdocument).
   - Documents are private: only the provider and admins get them, as download links that expire after 30 minutes. Don't store the links; fetch them again.

4. **Submit for verification** with [`submitProviderForVerification`](#submitproviderforverification). The status becomes `PENDING`, and a confirmation email is sent.
   - The server doesn't require documents, so require them in the app before enabling the button.
   - Errors: `ALREADY_PENDING`, `ALREADY_VERIFIED`, `INCOMPLETE_PROFILE`.
   - [`myVerificationStatus`](#myverificationstatus) returns `status`, `canSubmit` and a ready-made `message`.

5. **Wait for approval.** An admin calls [`approveProvider`](#approveprovider) or [`rejectProvider`](#rejectprovider).
   - The provider is told by email, an in-app notification (`VERIFICATION_APPROVED` or `VERIFICATION_REJECTED`) and a push. Only a `PENDING` profile can be approved (`NOT_PENDING`).
   - Check [`myVerificationStatus`](#myverificationstatus) when the app opens or comes to the foreground.

   | `verificationStatus` | Meaning | Show |
   |---|---|---|
   | `UNVERIFIED` | Never submitted | Checklist: profile, location, documents, then Submit |
   | `PENDING` | Waiting for an admin | "Under review, usually 1 to 2 business days" |
   | `VERIFIED` | Approved | Service management and bookings |
   | `REJECTED` | Not approved; the reason was emailed and is in `providerProfile.rejectionReason` | "Not approved", with `rejectionReason` and a way to update the details and submit again (`canSubmit` is true) |

6. **Create a service and get it approved.**
   1. Pick a category from [`categories`](#categories).
   2. Call [`createService`](#createservice). The provider must be verified (`PROVIDER_NOT_VERIFIED`), and the service starts as `DRAFT`. Rules:
      - `name`: 2 to 100 characters.
      - `description`: 10 to 10,000 characters.
      - `price`: in naira, up to 2 decimal places.
      - `duration`: in minutes.
      - Name and description can't contain blocked words or contact details.
      - The category must exist and be active (`CATEGORY_NOT_FOUND`, `CATEGORY_INACTIVE`).
      - When terms acceptance is required, the current terms must be accepted.
   3. Add up to 10 images with [`uploadServiceImages`](#uploadserviceimages).
   4. Call [`submitServiceForApproval`](#submitserviceforapproval), from `DRAFT` or `INACTIVE`. The status becomes `PENDING_APPROVAL`.
   5. An admin approves with [`approveService`](#approveservice), making it `ACTIVE` and bookable, or rejects it with [`rejectService`](#rejectservice), which sends it back to `DRAFT` with the reason in `rejectionReason`. [`suspendService`](#suspendservice) makes a service `SUSPENDED`, with the reason in `suspensionReason`. The provider gets an in-app notification (`SERVICE_APPROVED`, `SERVICE_REJECTED` or `SERVICE_SUSPENDED`) and a push for each decision.

   ```graphql
   mutation CreateService($input: CreateServiceInput!) {
     createService(input: $input) {
       id
       name
       price
       duration
       status
     }
   }
   ```
   Variables:
   ```json
   {
     "input": {
       "categoryId": "66e2a100c3b2a10012ab3001",
       "name": "Deep home cleaning",
       "description": "Full clean of kitchen, bathrooms, bedrooms and living areas, including inside cupboards.",
       "price": 15000,
       "duration": 240
     }
   }
   ```

   | Service `status` | Bookable | What the provider can do |
   |---|---|---|
   | `DRAFT` | No | Edit, add images, submit |
   | `PENDING_APPROVAL` | No | Wait, or set it back to `DRAFT` with [`updateService`](#updateservice) |
   | `ACTIVE` | Yes | Edit (it stays live, and admins get an automatic report to check), or set `INACTIVE` to hide it |
   | `INACTIVE` | No | Submit again to go live |
   | `SUSPENDED` | No | Contact support. Other fields can still be edited, but the status can't be changed (`SERVICE_SUSPENDED`) and it can't be submitted again. An admin reinstates it with [`approveService`](#approveservice), which makes it `ACTIVE`. |

   [`deleteService`](#deleteservice) only works on a service that has never been booked (`HAS_BOOKINGS`); otherwise set it `INACTIVE`.

7. **Handle booking requests.**
   - A new request arrives as `booking:created`, an in-app `BOOKING_CREATED` notification and a push (`action: new`). Refetch [`providerBookings`](#providerbookings) with `status: PENDING` when one arrives and when the app opens, and use [`providerBookingStats`](#providerbookingstats) for badge counts.
   - Accept with [`acceptBooking`](#acceptbooking), or decline with [`rejectBooking`](#rejectbooking). The reason is shown to the customer. Accepting fails with `BOOKING_NOT_ALLOWED` if either person has blocked the other since the request.
   - Both only work while the booking is `PENDING`. The server doesn't check for clashing bookings.

   ```graphql
   query IncomingRequests {
     providerBookings(filters: { status: PENDING }, pagination: { page: 1, limit: 20 }) {
       total
       items {
         id
         scheduledDate
         scheduledTime
         address
         city
         notes
         totalAmount
         service { name }
         user { firstName lastName }
       }
     }
   }
   ```

8. **Wait for payment.**
   - When the customer pays, the provider gets a push and an in-app `PAYMENT_RECEIVED` notification ("Payment Secured"), with no socket event.
   - The booking's `payment.status` becomes `COMPLETED`.
   - Until 24 hours before the scheduled time the customer can still cancel. The provider then gets `booking:cancelled`.

9. **Do the job.**
   - [`startService`](#startservice) moves the booking from `ACCEPTED` to `IN_PROGRESS`. It returns `PAYMENT_REQUIRED` until the customer has paid.
   - [`completeService`](#completeservice) moves `IN_PROGRESS` to `COMPLETED`. Neither operation checks the scheduled time.
   - A provider can't cancel an accepted booking. They can ask support to cancel it, or open a dispute.

10. **Earnings.**
    - **When the provider is paid:** 24 hours after the customer confirms, or 7 days after completion without a confirmation.
    - **What happens then:** the provider's share goes into their wallet as a `SERVICE_EARNING` credit, with an in-app notification ("Payment Released!") and no push.
    - **Where to show it:**
      - [`myWallet`](#mywallet): `balance` is what can be withdrawn.
      - [`myPendingEarnings`](#mypendingearnings): `availableNow` is what can be withdrawn now (the wallet balance, or 0 while a withdrawal is open). `totalPending` is earnings not yet in the wallet (the same as `myWallet.pendingBalance`), `pendingClearance` is the part still held, and `nextAvailableDate` is the next release date.
      - [`myEarnings`](#myearnings): `totalEarnings` and `thisMonthEarnings` add up the provider's share of paid bookings, including money still held. `commissionRate` is the rate actually charged on the provider's paid bookings (the current rate if they have none).
      - History: [`providerPayments`](#providerpayments), [`myEarningsReport`](#myearningsreport) and [`myWalletTransactions`](#mywallettransactions).

11. **Add a bank account.**
    1. Let the provider pick a bank from [`banks`](#banks). [`suggestBankFromAccountNumber`](#suggestbankfromaccountnumber) shortlists banks from the 10-digit number's check digit; it's only a hint, and microfinance banks are never suggested.
    2. Show the account name from [`verifyBankAccount`](#verifybankaccount). The account number must be 10 digits.
    3. Save with [`addBankAccount`](#addbankaccount). It reuses a verification of the same account from the last 15 minutes, or verifies it again. The first account becomes the default, and adding the same account twice fails (`DUPLICATE_ACCOUNT`).
    - **Limit:** 5 Paystack lookups per user in an hour (`RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, with `extensions.resetIn`). Invalid input, duplicates and an account verified in the last 15 minutes don't count.
    - **Manage:** [`myBankAccounts`](#mybankaccounts) and [`setDefaultBankAccount`](#setdefaultbankaccount). [`removeBankAccount`](#removebankaccount) fails while a withdrawal is open (`PENDING_WITHDRAWALS`) or an active payout schedule uses the account (`IN_USE_BY_PAYOUT_SCHEDULE`).

12. **Withdraw** with [`requestWithdrawal`](#requestwithdrawal), or set a payout schedule with [`setPayoutSchedule`](#setpayoutschedule). See [Wallet, earnings and withdrawals](#wallet-earnings-and-withdrawals).

13. **Switch the active role** with [`switchActiveRole`](#switchactiverole), to `SERVICE_USER` or `SERVICE_PROVIDER`; [`myActiveRole`](#myactiverole) reads it.
    - **What it is:** a setting on the account, shared by all devices. It doesn't change the token or the role, and the server doesn't enforce it.
    - **Effect:** provider operations work in either mode, and a provider can book other providers' services in either mode. Use it to choose which home screen to show.
    - **Errors:** `ALREADY_IN_ROLE`, `NOT_PROVIDER`, `INVALID_ROLE`.

### Booking lifecycle

| Status | Meaning | Next status: who, with which operation | Show |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PENDING` | Requested; waiting for the provider | `ACCEPTED`: provider, [`acceptBooking`](#acceptbooking). `REJECTED`: provider, [`rejectBooking`](#rejectbooking). `CANCELLED`: customer, [`cancelBooking`](#cancelbooking), or admin, [`adminCancelBooking`](#admincancelbooking). | Customer: "Waiting for the provider", with Edit and Cancel. Provider: Accept and Decline. |
| `ACCEPTED` | Accepted; waiting for payment, then the job | `IN_PROGRESS`: provider, [`startService`](#startservice), only once paid. `CANCELLED`: customer until 24 hours before the start, or admin. `DISPUTED`: either party, [`createDispute`](#createdispute). | Customer: "Pay now" until paid, then "Booked for <date>". Provider: "Waiting for payment", then "Start job". |
| `REJECTED` | Declined by the provider. Final. | None | `cancellationReason`, and an option to book someone else |
| `IN_PROGRESS` | The job has started | `COMPLETED`: provider, [`completeService`](#completeservice). `DISPUTED`: either party. `CANCELLED`: admin only. | Customer: "In progress". Provider: "Mark as done". |
| `COMPLETED` | The provider says the job is done | Stays `COMPLETED` when the customer confirms ([`confirmServiceDelivery`](#confirmservicedelivery)) and when the payment is released. `DISPUTED`: either party, until the payment is due for release (`paymentReleaseAt`, or 7 days after `completedAt` if the customer never confirms). A Super Admin full refund ([`processRefund`](#processrefund)) leaves it `COMPLETED` with its payment `REFUNDED`; nothing is released. | Customer: Confirm, Report a problem, Review.
